title: Use of dual-position and high-radioactivity 14C labeling, high-resolution mass spectrometry for pesticide transformation in vegetable: Uptake and metabolism of quinotrione in cabbage
abstract: 4-Hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPPD) is a critical target for herbicides. Excessive herbicide use causes environmental and health issues. Currently, limited information is available on the fate of the new HPPD inhibitor quinotrione in vegetables. This study employs dual-position and high-radioactivity 14 C labeling combined with high-resolution mass spectrometry (DP-HA- 14 C-HRMS) to investigate the uptake and metabolism of quinotrione ([quinazoline-2- 14 C]- and [cyclohexene-4- 14 C]-quinotrione) in Chinese flower cabbage. Results showed that 24.7-27.4 % of 14 C-quinotrione was accumulated in cabbage after 20 days. 14 C-quinotrione was primarily concentrated in roots (132.4-138.3 mg kg -1 ) and does not easily transport to edible parts (9.6-11.3 mg kg -1 ). In cabbage, 80 % of quinotrione was degraded into eight metabolites, and the identification process of two metabolites depended on the labeling location. The metabolic profile involved hydroxylation, dehydrogenation, denitrification, nitration, glycosylation, dexylene, and demethylation. The findings significantly advance our understanding of quinotrione's behavior in vegetables, with important implications for environmental and food safety risk assessments.

title: Comparative analysis of nutrition quality and volatile compounds in mature European and Asian red pears
abstract: Red pear is popular due to its bright colors and nutritional benefits. At present, there are few studies on the difference in quality characteristics between European and Asian red pears. The findings revealed that European red pears were distinguished by elevated sugar and acid levels, high concentrations of total phenolics and flavonoids, and vivid red coloration. The vivid red coloration was primarily attributable to the substantial amassment of cyanidin. In the pulp and peel of 10 red pear varieties, 43 and 51 volatile compounds were detected, respectively. Partial least squares discriminant analysis and correlation network analysis results indicated that Acetate esters were the primary contributors to the aroma differences between European and Asian red pear. Also, esters exhibited the strongest correlation with sugar and organic acid. This research offers insights into the quality attributes of diverse red pear varieties, potentially enhancing elite red pear germplasm resources.

title: Metabolomic and transcriptomic profiles reveal the mechanism of browning inhibition of Pueraria lobata by heat treatment
abstract: This study investigated the mechanism of browning inhibition of Pueraria lobata by heat treatment (70 °C for 5 min) by analyzing its effects on polyphenol oxidase (PPO) activity, browning index, antioxidant activity, metabolite and gene expression profiles using physiological, metabolomic and transcriptomic approaches. Heat treatment inhibited PPO activity and delayed the browning of Pueraria lobata, while increasing free radical scavenging activity and total flavonoid content. Metabolomic analyses revealed that catechins, caffeic acid, tyrosine and coumaric acid might be the major metabolites associated with the browning of Pueraria lobata, whereas flavonoid and isoflavonoid metabolites might be beneficial for delaying browning. Multi-omics analysis revealed that the tyrosine metabolism and isoflavone biosynthesis pathways were enriched and played crucial regulatory roles in browning. This study provides a practical strategy for improving quality in post-harvest processing and deep processing of Pueraria lobata. Future research need focus on the spatial variation analysis of these browning-related metabolites in Pueraria lobata.

title: Impacts of backslopping fermentation on the hierarchical structure, physicochemical properties and digestibility of mung bean starch
abstract: Backslopping fermentation (BF) is a traditional method that modulates the physicochemical properties and digestibility of starch. Our study investigated the impact of BF on mung bean starch (MBS). The results showed that BF reduced the particle size of MBS and facilitated the formation of surface pores in the starch granules. Furthermore, notable aggregation of the starch occurred after 6 days of fermentation. The relative crystallinity and R 1047 / 1022 values of the fermented MBS initially decreased and then increased over time. Short-term BF significantly disrupted the semi-crystalline lamellae and double-helical structures of MBS, whereas long-term fermentation had the opposite effect. These structural changes resulted in decreased solubility and peak viscosity but increased final viscosity. MBS demonstrated strong slow digestibility after 6 days of fermentation. Overall, BF effectively modifies the structure and functionality of MBS, providing an environmentally friendly method for producing MBS with improved quality and potential health benefits.

title: The mechanism of β-ionone enhancing the sweet taste of phloridzin
abstract: In our previous study, phloridzin ('phl') and β-ionone ('bet') was identified as key contributors to the taste and sweet aroma of Camellia nanchuanica black tea, respectively. To study the effects of 'bet' on the sweetness of 'phl' and the specific perception mechanisms via retronasal and orthonasal pathways, we first analyzed the interactions between various concentrations of 'bet' (bet-8bet) and 'phl' (phl-8phl) using quantitative descriptive analysis. Our findings revealed that 'bet' odor significantly enhanced the sweetness of 'phl' (phl-8phl) through both retronasal and orthonasal pathways, particularly at concentrations of 2bet or greater. Subsequently, we observed that retronasal 'bet' odor sweetened 'phl' by increasing the stability between 'phl' and Taste 1 Receptor Member 3 (TAS1R3) based on determination of calcium signal and molecular dynamics simulations. However, orthonasal 'bet' odor likely heightened the perception of 'phl"s sweet taste by activating the left temporal regions of the brain, which are correlated with positive emotion.

title: Reactions between dicarbonyls and food proteins: when lipid oxidation and the maillard reaction meet protein oxidation
abstract: Over the recent decades, clear evidence showed that protein carbonylation has a significant influence on food quality and human health. The chemical nature and mechanism of food protein carbonylation remain poorly understood. One obstacle is the routine DNPH method lacks accuracy and consistency and it is unable to distinguish between primary and secondary carbonylation since DNPH can label both of them. Another obstacle is that within food systems, two major reactions (the Maillard reaction and lipid oxidation) can lead to generation of a range of reactive substances which interact with protein and add complexity to protein carbonylation. This review focuses on the mechanisms and factors governing the chemistry behind protein carbonylation in connection with lipid oxidation and the Maillard reaction. The consequences of the chemical and structural changes in proteins will also be covered. This review will shed light on the complicated mechanism of protein carbonylation in foods and empower future studies in this area.

title: Cellulose cryogel microparticles increase gas permeation of carnauba wax-based edible coating for jujube preservation application
abstract: Wax coating is an important preservation method extending jujube's shelf life. Although wax-based coatings provide a moisture resistant and physical microbial barrier, their dense structure excessively restricts the CO 2 and O 2 permeation, leading to anaerobic respiration and off-flavor. To increase the CO 2 and O 2 permeation of wax-based coating while minimizing its impact on inherent properties, microcrystalline cellulose cryogel particles (CCPs) were developed and incorporated into carnauba wax-based edible coating (CCPCW) creating micro gas channel. 1.00 % CCPCW increased the CO 2 and O 2 permeability by 190 % and 227 %, compared to CW, respectively. The inherent properties of CW, moisture and physical fungal barrier were retained. Finally, the jujube preservation performance of CCPCW was conducted. The CCPCW reduced the acetaldehyde and ethanol production of jujubes by 34.79 % and 15.81 %, respectively. These findings underscore the potential of CCPCW as an effective edible coating for mitigating off-flavors in jujube preservation.

title: Value-adding Okara via Monascus purpureus solid-state fermentation: Microstructural remodeling, metabolite enrichment, and bioactivity enhancement
abstract: Okara, the main by-product of soybean processing, is rich in bioactive compounds yet remains underutilized due to unfavorable flavor, gritty texture, poor digestibility, rapid spoilage, and disposal concerns. To valorize, this study explored upcycling okara via solid-state fermentation with M. purpureus over 25 days to improve its structural, chemical, and functional transformations. Comprehensive analyses by SEM, UPLC-MS, and GC–MS demonstrated a honeycomb-like porous surface with enhanced water-holding, water-swelling, oil-absorption, and cholesterol-binding capacities, metabolic shifts, and volatiles dominated by buttery 2,3-butanediol rather than off-flavors. Total phenolics, flavonoids, and saponins increased 2.27-, 3.08-, and 1.70-fold, respectively, while ergosterol, monacolin K, and l -carnitine accumulated to 688.85, 24.96, and 332.21 mg/kg, with no citrinin detected. β-glucosidase activity converted isoflavone glycosides into bioactive aglycones. Functional assays showed improved antioxidant activity, α-glucosidase inhibition, and reduced lipid accumulation in 3 T3-L1 cells. These findings highlight a sustainable, citrinin-free approach to upcycle okara into a multifunctional nutraceutical ingredient. • Okara was upcycled using solid-state fermentation with Monascus purpureus KCCM 13460P. • Isoflavone glycosides were converted into their aglycones by producing β-glucosidase activity. • Ergosterol, monacolin K, and l -carnitine were produced during fermentation. • Fermented okara enhances antioxidant capacity and α-glucosidase inhibition. • 2,3-butanediol, which imparts buttery and creamy flavors, was a key volatile in fermented okara.

title: Effect of mammalian gelatin types on the preparation and properties of fish oil-loaded genipin-crosslinked gelatin-alginate powders
abstract: This study investigated the effect of three types of mammalian gelatins (Porcine skin gelatin, PSG; bovine bone gelatin, BBG; bovine skin gelatin, BSG) on the preparation and properties of fish oil-loaded intra-particularly genipin-crosslinked gelatin‑sodium alginate (SA) complex coacervated powders. At comparable particle sizes, BBG-based powders exhibited lower oil loading yield (44.7 % vs. 63.0 %-67.5 %), lower oil loading capacity (18.8 % vs. 26.5 %-28.4 %), lower encapsulation efficiency (88.7 % vs. 97.1 %-98.2 %), higher peroxide values (774 vs. 517-547 mmol/kg oil) under Schaal oven condition (63 °C), and higher in vitro accumulative fatty acid digestion release (e.g., 120 min: 46.3 % vs. 32.2 %-34.0 %) than the other two gelatins-based powders. It implied that skin-derived gelatins were superior to bone-derived gelatin as wall materials for oil encapsulation via complex coacervation. This work provided valuable insights into the relationship between the molecular weights of mammalian gelatins and the properties of oil powders.

title: Droplet-based amperometric sensor for iodate in table salt using screen-printed carbon electrode
abstract: The application of electrochemical methods for iodate determination was investigated using a bare screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE). A rapid, precise, and accurate amperometric iodate sensing strategy was established with this SPCE. The method employs a low-pH acid solution as the solvent for table salt and requires only 60 μL of sample solution. Cyclic voltammetry confirmed the electrocatalytic reduction of iodate, yielding a sensitivity of -0.596 μA/(mg/L). Under optimized amperometric conditions, two linear ranges were obtained: 1-10 mg/L (LOD = 0.049 mg/L) and 10-250 mg/L (LOD = 0.21 mg/L). Analysis of real salt samples showed no significant difference compared with the reference method (p > 0.05). The use of a bare SPCE thus provides a low-cost, green, and practical platform for electrochemical determination of iodate in table salt, offering potential as the basis for an electrochemical rapid test kit (RTK).

title: A multi-omics investigation of annual variation patterns in phenolic and ester compounds in red wine and their association with meteorological factors
abstract: The quality of red wine is influenced by interannual climate variations in grape regions. However, the key grape growth stages are unclear. Our multi-omics research indicates that the flowering-to-coloring stage of grapes is an important period affecting the quality of red wine. The cumulative precipitation during flowering-to-coloring stage (-57.22 %) was negatively correlated with total phenol content, total flavonoid content, and FRAP antioxidant capacity (+69.18-781.25 %). 72 phenolic compounds were identified in red wine by UPLC-MS/MS. The abundance of anthocyanins was positively correlated with color intensity, %red, and %blue. Additionally, the levels of phenolic compounds were negatively correlated with cumulative precipitation during grape flowering-to-coloring stage. Furthermore, 19 ester and 10 alcohol compounds were identified by HS-SPME-GC-MS. The levels of esters were negatively correlated with cumulative precipitation during grape coloring-to-ripening stage. Principal component analysis further confirmed that lower precipitation may intensify astringency, fruity aroma, color intensity, and red-blue hues of red wines.

title: Eco-efficient extraction of daidzein and genistein from soybean meal: Integrating enzymatic hydrolysis and HIUS-PLE
abstract: Isoflavones are a subclass of flavonoids with diverse biological activities, and their aglycone forms, daidzein and genistein, are targeted due to their higher bioavailability and bioaccessibility. This study applied high-intensity ultrasound-assisted pressurized liquid extraction (HIUS-PLE), optimized by a Box-Behnken design and Response Surface Methodology, to maximize aglycone yields from soybean meal. Enzymatic hydrolysis with tannase was further integrated into the HIUS-PLE system to convert conjugated isoflavones into aglycones. Under optimal extraction conditions, the process yielded 582.5 μg/g aglycones. After enzymatic hydrolysis integration, this content increased by 178 %, reaching 1620.96 μg/g within 75 min. The method proved rapid, eco-efficient, and scalable, suitable for food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications. The Path2Green sustainability assessment scored +0.192, highlighting strengths in solvent selection and biomass valorization, while indicating opportunities to improve energy efficiency and circularity.

title: Deep eutectic solvent-assisted aqueous extraction of pectin and essential oil from Citrus reticulata peel: Physicochemical characteristics and emulsifying properties
abstract: Present study establishes a deep eutectic solvents (DES)-assisted biorefinery strategy for the valorization of Citrus reticulata peel. Choline chloride (CC)/lactic acid (LA) and CC/glycerol (G) pretreatments of citrus peel facilitated hot water extraction of large amounts of pectin. Pectin (CC/LA-CP and CC/G-CP) extracted following CC/LA or CC/G pretreatment had a higher Mw and are rich in homogalacturonan (HG). CC/LA-CP classified as high-methoxyl pectin, whereas CC/G-CP was low-methoxyl pectin. Among six DESs, CC/LA pretreatment of citrus peel following hydro-distillation extraction yielded the highest essential oil (CEO, 3.19 ± 0.02 %) with 32 types of aromatic compounds. O/W emulsions prepared with pectin and CEO showed that the structural features of pectin affected droplet size and stability of emulsions across varying durations, temperatures, ionic strengths and pH conditions. Finally, CEO emulsions were proved to be antibacterial and antioxidative. This DES-assisted biorefinery approach enables the recovery of valuable pectin and CEO to form functional emulsions.

title: A comparison of micronutrient elements in cooked white, brown and parboiled rice using synchrotron micro-X-ray fluorescence imaging
abstract: Rice is a staple food for over half the world's population. This study uniquely investigates the spatial distribution of key micronutrients (Cu, Mn, Fe, Zn) in cooked brown, white, and parboiled rice using Synchrotron Micro-X-ray Fluorescence (sXRF) for the first time. Complementary analysis with Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) validates bulk elemental concentrations. Results from this dual-approach study reveal significantly higher micronutrient concentrations in brown rice compared to white or parboiled rice, with nutrients predominantly localised in the peripheral layers and minimal presence in the endosperm. Notably, sXRF imaging identified nutrient-rich pockets within the grain periphery, offering new perspectives on nutrient distribution beyond peripheral accumulation. Additional insights include the impact of rice section thickness (50 and 150 μm) and beam dwell times (0.5 and 30s) on sXRF sensitivity and resolution, highlighting trade-offs in detection capabilities, advancing our understanding of micronutrient localisation in cooked rice.

title: Bacteria-functionalized biochar promotes phthalate degradation and limits uptake in lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.)
abstract: The widespread use of plastics has led to the release of phthalic acid esters (PAEs), which pose risks to ecosystems and human health due to their persistence and bioaccumulation. This study evaluated biochar (BC) with immobilized bacteria as a remediation strategy for PAEs-contaminated agricultural soils. Biochar enhanced microbial activity and supported PAEs degradation. Bacillus subtilis showed the lowest metabolic activity, while Gordonia phthalatica , Patulibacter brassicae , and a mixed inoculum achieved ~70 % degradation efficiency. Indigenous soil microbes effectively degraded low molecular weight PAEs (72–75 %), but less efficiently targeted high molecular weight ones (54–68 %). Lettuce grown in treated soils showed no PAEs degradation products, suggesting effective containment and minimal plant translocation. Monomethyl phthalate was the primary biodegradation intermediate. These results highlight the potential of biochar combined with microbial consortia as a dual-function solution: adsorption and biodegradation, for removing phthalates from agricultural soil. • Biochar with immobilized bacteria increased PAEs biodegradation in the soil. • BC was a nutrient supplier and habitat for bacteria lowering PAEs content in lettuce. • Bacillus subtilis had the lowest metabolism rate for all tested phthalates. • Monomethyl phthalate was the primary biodegradation product of all PAEs in the soil. • Patulibacter brassicae had the highest efficiency in the decomposition of all PAEs.

title: Antioxidant properties of camel and bovine colostrum upon simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion: Peptide identification, molecular simulation and binding mechanism
abstract: This study assessed the digestibility, antioxidant properties and peptide released upon simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion (SIGID) of camel and bovine colostrum. After SIGID, significant increase in degree of protein hydrolysis (DH) was observed in camel and bovine colostrum as compared to undigested samples. 2,2-Diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) and 2,2′ -azino-bis (3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) radical scavenging activities showed a significant increase after SIGID. Peptides generated after SIGID were then identified using LCMS-QTOF and their interaction was studied with Kelch-Neh2 Complex (PDB: 2FLU ) using molecular docking and dynamic simulation method. The selected peptides (camel colostrum: FPLAP and EGGFDAKLMFIV; and bovine colostrum: PGPPGTPGPI and SLVYPFPGPI) formed stable interactions with Keap 1 protein having binding energy of −8.6 and − 8.1; and − 9.2 and − 9.2, respectively, thereby potentially activating the Keap 1-Nrf2 signalling pathway. Hence, this gives insight about the digestibility pattern and antioxidant properties of camel and bovine colostrum under SIGID conditions, demonstrating their potential use as an active ingredient in infant formula. • Simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion (SIGID) of camel and bovine colostrum. • Both samples showed good digestibility with variation in the digestion pattern. • Antioxidant activity and degree of hydrolysis increased after SIGID. • Molecular docking and dynamic simulation with Keap1 predicted antioxidant properties. • All peptides derived from camel colostrum digestion were non-toxic and non-allergenic.

title: Plasmonic silver nanorod-reinforced flexible polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel SERS sensors for ultrasensitive detection of food colorants in fruit juice
abstract: Excessive consumption of artificial food colorants can lead to potential health risks. There is an urgent need for a rapid and convenient method to detect residues of these artificial colorants. In this research, we developed a flexible AgNRs@PVA surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensor by uniformly depositing silver nanorods (AgNRs) onto the surface of a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel. Due to the three-dimensional high-density and uniform hot spots formed by the interwoven one-dimensional silver nanorods, the AgNRs@PVA hydrogel SERS substrate demonstrates outstanding detection sensitivity of 10 -11 M, good signal uniformity and exceptional storage stability for malachite green. In addition, the AgNRs@PVA hydrogel SERS substrate exhibits prominent detection sensitivity, achieving limits of 10 -7 M and 10 -6 M for the artificial food colorants of sunset yellow and carmine in fruit juice. Moreover, AgNRs@PVA SERS substrate also demonstrates satisfactory detection performance and practicality for analysis of artificial food colorants in commercial products.

title: Comparative analysis of enzymatic hydrolysis kinetics and bioactive peptide release during in vitro digestion of mycoprotein and conventional meat
abstract: This study compared the in vitro digestion kinetics and peptide release profiles of mycoprotein and conventional meat proteins. Mycoprotein showed significantly lower gastric digestibility (∼22 %) than pork and beef (>40 %, P < 0.05), due to its β-glucan-chitin cell wall barrier. However, during the intestinal phase, mycoprotein exhibited a 52 % increase in digestibility, surpassing meat's 42 %, and released a higher proportion of short peptides (<1900 Da). Rheological analysis revealed greater viscosity and shear sensitivity in mycoprotein chyme. Zeta potential and particle size data indicated a unique "aggregation-redispersion" pattern. Peptidomic analysis identified more stable and phase-persistent bioactive peptides (e.g., DPP-IV inhibitor GFW and α-glucosidase inhibitors YPL/YPY), with up to 12 % cross-phase retention. Ammonium sulfate fermentation enhanced essential amino acid levels and digestion efficiency, while ammonia water led to denser cell structures and lower peptide diversity. These findings highlight the structure-dependent, sustained-release digestion behavior of mycoprotein and its potential for functional food applications.

title: Metabolomic approach to explore the chemical composition and health benefits of macroalgae: A comprehensive study of Palmaria palmata, Ascophyllum nodosum, and Chondrus crispus
abstract: This study examined the biochemical composition and bioactivity of three macroalgae (seaweed) species: Palmaria palmata, Ascophyllum nodosum, and Chondrus crispus. Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy identified 18 metabolites, including amino and organic acids with significant interspecies variation. Inductively Coupled Plasma analysis showed high calcium (up to 49,340 mg/kg in C. crispus) and iron (728.9 mg/kg in C. crispus), with trace arsenic and lead present. High-Performance Liquid Chromatography detected carotenoids lutein (0.0105 mg/mL) and α-carotene (0.0010 mg/mL) in P. palmata. Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry revealed A. nodosum rich in oleic acid (57.3 %), P. palmata in palmitic acid (82.8 %), and C. crispus in myristic acid (48.7 %). Antioxidant assays showed C. crispus (IC₅₀ 5.33 mg/mL, DPPH) and A. nodosum (IC₅₀ 0.25 mg/mL, ABTS) had highest activity. Significant antibacterial inhibition zones (up to 4.67 mm) and 66.6 % biofilm reduction by C. crispus were observed. These macroalgae represent promising natural bioactive sources for food and health.

title: Comparative in vitro intestinal transport and bioactivity of peptides from wet- and dry-heated goat milk proteins after simulated infant digestion
abstract: This study investigated the digestion of proteins (12 mg/mL) in goat skimmed milk with casein-to-whey protein ratios of 80:20 and 40:60. The effects of dry and wet heating on peptide formation and peptides transport were studied in vitro. Peptide transport across the Caco-2 cell monolayer was largely determined by the peptide composition in the digesta. Some peptides were further cleaved during transport across the Caco-2 monolayer. Transport was associated with glycation, peptide length, and hydrophobicity; fewer peptides with advanced glycation were transported across the Caco-2 cell monolayer. Basolateral peptides were relatively shorter and more hydrophilic than digesta peptides, probably due to further proteolysis by Caco-2 cell-derived enzymes. Protein composition and heat treatment influenced the presence of bioactive peptides and linear epitopes in the basolateral compartment. This study highlights the importance of the casein:whey ratio in goat milk based infant formula and indicates dry heating could affect its nutritional quality.

title: Deciphering the role of endogenous polyphenols in the stability and rheological properties of walnut Oleosome emulsions
abstract: This study investigated the role of endogenous walnut pellicle polyphenols in modulating the stability and rheological behavior of walnut oleosome emulsions. Since polyphenols are predominantly concentrated in walnut pellicle, oleosomes were extracted from kernels with (WO) and without pellicle (PFWO). WO exhibited significantly higher polyphenol content and greater antioxidant capacity compared to PFWO. WO emulsions had smaller oil droplet sizes and more rigid interfacial layer as revealed by in situ confocal Raman spectroscopy. Rheological analyses demonstrated that both WO and PFWO emulsions displayed shear-thinning behavior, though WO demonstrated higher viscosity and viscoelasticity. Furthermore, WO emulsions exhibited enhanced resistance to ionic strength and thermal stress, along with improved physical and lipid oxidative stability compared to PFWO. These results indicate that native walnut polyphenols substantially enhance emulsion stability and rheological performance. This work advances the mechanistic understanding of polyphenol-oleosome interactions and supports the application of walnut oleosomes in clean-label food formulations.

title: Analysis of the mechanism of quality deterioration of egg yolk powder during storage from a multi-dimensional perspective
abstract: This study systematically elucidated the patterns of quality deterioration in egg yolk powder (EYP) during 60 days of accelerated storage under controlled conditions of (37 ± 0.5) °C and relative humidity maintained at (75 ± 5) %. The experiment found that with the extension of storage time, the sensory attributes and functional properties of EYP changed significantly: among the key functional indicators, solubility decreased by (39.02 ± 0.18) %, EAI decreased by (24.32 ± 1.79) %, and ESI increased by (50.02 ± 5.97) %. The internal water distribution showed characteristic phase changes. Large molecular lipid-protein complexes were formed internally. The analysis found that the synchronous oxidation of lipids and proteins is the core mechanism causing quality deterioration. By dynamically monitoring the changes in volatile substances, eight key differential volatile substances with stage-indicating functions were screened out. This conclusion provides theoretical support for the development of EYP with extended shelf life.

title: Non-destructive assessment of quality parameters in Javadi cv. Peach fruits using Vis/NIR spectroscopy and multiple regression analysis
abstract: This study aimed to non-destructively identify quality parameters in Javadi peaches. In this context, a capacitive array (CCD) spectroradiometer ranging from 350 to 1150 nm was employed for the nondestructive prediction of pH, titrable acid (TA), soluble solid-state (SSC), total phenol (TP), extract anthocyanin (Prance and Nesbitt). Utilizing multivariate partial least squares (PLS) regression models, both reference and degradation measurements were considered. Various spectral data processing techniques such as Savitsky-Goley smoothing (SG), first derivative (D1), incremental diffusivity correction (MSC), standard normal variate (SNV), and Baseline correction were applied individually and in combination (SG + MSC + D1) and (SG + Baseline) to forecast peach quality attributes. Model performance was assessed using the root mean square error of prediction (RMSEP), correlation coefficient (rp), and standard deviation ratio (SDR). Optimal models showed high accuracy for pH (raw spectra: RMSEP = 0.15, rp = 0.94, SDR = 3.0), moderate for TA (first derivative: RMSEP = 0.07, rp = 0.86, SDR = 2.29) and SSC (MSC: RMSEP = 1.17, rp = 0.85, SDR = 1.88), but lower for TP and EA (SDR < 1.5). This non-destructive approach offers rapid, cost-effective quality assessment compared to destructive methods.

title: Electropolymerized melamine on fluoride-free molten salt etching 2D niobium carbide MXene: A promising electrocatalyst for free radical antioxidant diphenylamine detection in food samples
abstract: This work reports a fluoride-free synthesis of Nb 2 CT x nanosheets using a molten salt and Lewis acid etching approach, offering a safer and more efficient exfoliation route. To enhance the functional performance of Nb 2 CT x , we developed an electropolymerisation method to coat its surface with nitrogen-rich polymelamine (PM), utilising a potentiodynamic technique in a Cl - -containing electrolyte. The Cl - ions facilitate the formation of NH 3 + and -NH 2 intermediates from melamine monomers, which subsequently interact with the oxygen-containing functional groups of Nb 2 CT x , leading to a stable PM@Nb 2 CT x composite. The fabricated PM@Nb 2 CT x electrode was applied to detect diphenylamine (DPA• + ) sensitively, a chemical commonly used to prevent postharvest fruit damage during overseas storage. Amperometric studies demonstrated that the PM@Nb 2 CT x sensor offers an excellent detection limit of 161 pM with a wide linear range (1-8 nM). Results showcasing the potential of this material platform for real-time DPA detection and broader applications in food monitoring.

title: A comprehensive story of pea peptides and pea polyphenols: Research status, existing problems, and development trends
abstract: Pea peptides and pea polyphenols have gained much attention for their potential nutrition and health benefits, such as antibacterial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and hypoglycemic, showing great application potential in developing functional and healthy food. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the preparation technologies, bioactive activities and potential application fields, describing the research status, existing problems and development trends of pea peptides and pea polyphenols. Besides, the antioxidant, antibacterial, antidiabetic, and blood pressure lowering activities of pea peptides, as well as the current research status of delivery systems were mainly summarized and discussed. Additionally, the combination of pea peptides/polyphenols with other nutrients to develop new functional food ingredients will spark a trend in the development of plant-based nutritional health foods. This review will provide clear research ideas for further in-depth research and application of pea peptides and pea polyphenols, and point out the direction for scientific researchers committed to pea research.

title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum-mediated bioconversion of blue honeysuckle juice amplifies phenolics to inhibit xanthine oxidase and reshapes volatile metabolome
abstract: Fermentation-mediated biotransformation represents an effective strategy to enhance the bioactivity of functional juices. This study examined the inhibitory effects of blue honeysuckle juice fermented with eight Lactiplantibacillus plantarum strains on xanthine oxidase (XO) activity. Fermentation significantly enhances the XO inhibition capacity of blue honeysuckle juice. LC-MS analysis revealed substantial increases in six key phenolic compounds with XO inhibitory activity: C3G (IC 50 = 115.28 μmol/L), cyanidin-3,5-diglucoside (IC 50 = 116.34 μmol/L), peonidin-3-glucoside (IC 50 = 105.34 μmol/L), 3-caffeoylquinic acid (IC 50 = 250.35 μmol/L), quercetin (IC 50 = 88.75 μmol/L), and catechin (IC 50 = 110 μmol/L). Molecular simulations elucidated the inhibitory mechanism through stabilized ligand-XO interactions involving hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces, and π-σ interactions over 100 ns trajectories. Notably, fermentation also reduced the aldehyde content, correlating with improved sensory profile. These findings demonstrate that Lactiplantibacillus plantarum fermentation enhances the biological activity and organoleptic properties of blue honeysuckle juice, providing mechanistic insights and practical strategies for developing functional beverages.

title: A preliminary approach to increase oxidative stability in wines: the addition of sacrificial amino acids naturally occurring in wine to reduce Strecker aldehydes formation
abstract: Strecker aldehydes (SA) are oxidation-related odorants, a menace to wine's ageing capacity and aromatic quality. To date, no universal solution exists to drastically reduce their formation beyond a meticulous oxygen management, which is difficult to control during commercialisation. These aldehydes mainly form via reaction of their corresponding Strecker amino acids with α-dicarbonyls. Therefore, this study aims to decrease their production by the addition of naturally occurring amino acids in wine, that might reduce the availability of α-dicarbonyls. Different accelerated oxidation procedures are performed on model wine and wine matrixes with sacrificial amino acids and SA are quantified and compared against their control. The additions of 4 mM of L-Tyrosine (Tyr) and L-Aspartic acid (Asp) reduce production rates up to 15 % in spiked wines or 7–8 % in rosé for 3-methylbutanal, methional and phenylacetaldehyde. This study sheds light on a promising technique for reducing SA in wine and potentially increasing its longevity. • Wine-naturally occurring amino acids are added to reduce Strecker aldehydes formation. • Most significant reductions are obtained when tyrosine and aspartic acid are added. • Although significant, the sensory impact of these additions would need to be studied.

title: Metabolic fate of polyphenols in LAB-fermented kiwifruit juice: A comparative study of single and mixed cultures with targeted metabolomics and enzymatic evidence
abstract: This study investigated the biotransformation of free and bound polyphenols in kiwifruit juice fermented by single LAB strains (LA3 or LP2) and the mixed culture ALP2 (LA3 + LP2). Results showed that fermentation significantly increased free polyphenol content and antioxidant capacity, with LP2 exhibiting the strongest effect. Ten biomarkers, including protocatechuic acid and epicatechin, were identified through targeted metabolomic analysis. Enzyme activity assays revealed that LP2 had the highest PAL and PPO activities, promoting the conversion of phenolic precursors, while LA3 showed the strongest β-GC and 4CL activities, enhancing the release and synthesis of flavonoids. In the ALP2 group, polyphenol levels were mostly intermediate, indicating limited synergy from competition and overlapping enzyme functions. However, specific metabolites such as 3-hydroxybenzoic acid were significantly upregulated, suggesting possible activation of complementary pathways. These findings provide new insights into the distinct roles of LAB strains in polyphenol bioconversion and highlight the metabolic complexity of co-fermentation systems.

title: Complete loss of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate in wheat during simulated gastric digestion
abstract: Folate deficiency affects over one billion people globally, driving widespread cereal fortification programs. 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF), the predominant natural folate form, is emerging as a safer alternative to traditional folic acid for fortification. However, conflicting reports exist regarding its digestive stability. Here we demonstrate that 5-MTHF undergoes an apparent complete loss in wheat matrices during simulated gastric digestion. This loss occurred across all wheat fractions tested and exhibited concentration-dependent kinetics, with folate retention improving from undetectable levels to 80 % when wheat flour concentration was reduced fifty-fold. Ascorbic acid provided substantial protection, whereas gallic acid showed negligible effects. Nitrogen purging failed to prevent the phenomenon, and enzymatic analysis of digestion residues confirms that it was not attribute to simple physical absorption. These findings suggest endogenous wheat components promote a rapid, largely oxygen-insensitive loss of 5-MTHF, challenging existing fortification paradigms and underscoring the necessity for protective strategies in cereal-based folate delivery systems.

title: Deep learning-based fine-tuning transfer improves the generalizability of tea component prediction using miniature near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Model accuracies for predicting tea components using near-infrared spectroscopy are often constrained by sample type. Herein, spectral data from four tea types (green, black, oolong, and yellow) were collected using a low-cost, miniature near-infrared spectrometer. Various strategies were explored to develop generalized predictive models for catechins and caffeine across different tea types. Local models trained on single tea types were unable to accurately predict the samples from other types. Although global models that incorporated diverse tea samples demonstrated improved performance, their accuracies remained unacceptable. To address this limitation, a deep learning-based fine-tuning strategy was implemented, enabling the transfer of accuracy from local models to other tea types. Fine-tuning the convolutional and fully connected layers of pre-trained models resulted in accurate predictions of catechin and caffeine content in all tea samples, outperforming traditional transfer component analysis. This study presents a generalizable and cost-effective method for the determination of tea components.

title: Maillard reaction-mediated “glycation armor” in fermented soy protein isolate: Elucidating gel structural and oral processing behavior
abstract: This study modified fermented soybean protein isolate through Maillard reaction to investigate its gel structure and oral processing properties. Spectroscopic analysis revealed that Maillard reaction conferred enhanced structural and thermal stability to the gel through the formation of "glycation armor" via covalent crosslinking. Rheological results demonstrated that the synergy of Maillard reaction and fermentation significantly improved the gel's molecular network strength, absolute modulus (25.39 ± 2.78 Pa·s), and strain recovery ratio (62.41 ± 1.14 %). Oral perception evaluation indicated that the 4 h Maillard reaction-treated sample exhibited markedly enhanced umami and richness, closely correlated with the accumulation of Maillard reaction-derived compounds and the reduction of beany off-flavor components. The 4 h Maillard reaction-treated sample showed an increased friction coefficient, with lubrication properties that further improved upon artificial saliva addition, suggesting saliva-mediated optimization. This work provides novel insights into the synergistic design of gel structure and oral perception in plant-based foods.

title: Multifunctional pea protein-corn starch films with green tea polyphenols: enhanced antimicrobial activity in beef packaging
abstract: The use of biorenewable resources for the development of active packaging films, which can improve meat preservation, has significant importance. Composite films were developed using pea protein isolate, corn starch and green tea polyphenols (GTP). Molecular docking simulation evaluated the interaction mechanisms of GTP's bioactives with film matrices and assessed their antimicrobial mechanism. Atomic force microscopy revealed notable morphological alterations in active films. ATR-FTIR and XRD assessed molecular interactions and crystallinity, indicating hydrogen bonding among film components. GTP addition improved tensile strength and barrier properties against oxygen, water, and UV. A significant differences (p < 0.05) in the films' water-related properties, opacity, and color values were observed based on GTP concentration. The films demonstrated excellent antioxidant and antibacterial properties. The shelf life of beef was extended by up to 72 h through delayed microbial spoilage. This study provides insights into developing composite films with enhanced antibacterial activity through bioactive components for improved food packaging.

title: Evaluation of EDCs (phthalates, bisphenols, parabens, and benzophenones) in coffee: cross-sectional study in Algiers
abstract: Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are emerging environmental pollutants. The present study focused on evaluating the concentrations of EDCs in packed coffee. Among 12 investigated EDCs, only DEP, DEHP, DnBP, BPA, and BPF were found in packed coffee (20 %, 40 %, 80 %, 20 %, and 20 %, respectively). The mean values ranged from 0.230 ng/g for BPA to 23.214 ng/g for DnBP. DnBP was the most frequently detected EDC in coffee powder (60 %), followed by DEP, DEHP, BPA, and BPF (20 % each). Migration assessment showed that DEHP, DnBP, and BPF amounts were significantly higher after coffee preparation in the traditional coffee maker (2.515 vs 2.192 ng/mL, 1.845 vs 1.491 ng/mL, and 0.177 vs < LD ng/mL). The levels of phthalates and BPA did not exceed the specific migration limits (SMLs) and the estimated daily intake (EDI) to EDCs were low. Hazard quotients (HQs) were below 1.0 for general and highly exposed populations.

title: Revealing the polyphenol modulation mechanism for in vitro gastric digestion properties of myofibrillar proteins via noncovalent interaction
abstract: The in vitro gastric digestion of myofibrillar proteins (MPs) in the presence of polyphenols (protocatechuic acid (PCA), caffeic acid (CFA), and apigenin (AP)) was investigated. Results showed that polyphenols bound with pepsin to decrease the enzyme activity, whose binding capacity were correlated well with the degree of hydrolysis (DH). The compete binding between MPs and pepsin with polyphenols altered the protein gastric digestion. Compared with the control, the PCA was priority to bound with pepsin and displayed a lower DH of 8.15 % at low concentration (20 μmol/g protein), while CFA and AP may interact with MPs first to cause structure loosen and facilitate the proteolysis of pepsin, as manifested by a higher DH value, lower H 0 , greater red-shift of λ max and smaller particle size under CLSM. However, the extra CFA and AP may bound to pepsin and exerted a strong inhibitory effect to decrease the protein hydrolysis with increasing the addition of polyphenols (100 μmol/g protein).

title: Effect of epigallocatechin-3-gallate modification combined with mechanical pretreatment on the structural characteristics and Pickering emulsion stability of rice bran protein-polysaccharide-phenol natural complex
abstract: To enhance the use of insoluble rice bran protein-polysaccharide-phenol natural complex (IRBPPP) as Pickering emulsion stabilizers in the food industry, IRBPPP was modified using epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) addition (0, 3.125, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50 mg/g) and mechanical pretreatment methods (shear, ultrasonic, high-pressure homogenization, and combined mechanical treatment). Mechanical pretreatment promoted both covalent and noncovalent binding of EGCG to IRBPPP. Compared to the Pickering emulsion stability of IRBPPP without EGCG modification and mechanical pretreatment (creaming index: 27.7%; ζ-potential: -18.7 mV), a moderate concentration of EGCG (12.5 mg/g) and combined mechanical treatment synergistically improved the emulsion stability of IRBPPP (creaming index: 2.5%; ζ-potential: -29.7 mV). The Pickering emulsion stability was highly correlated (P < 0.01) with the ζ-potential, surface hydrophobicity, and protein flexibility of the IRBPPP. Overall, moderate EGCG modification combined with appropriate mechanical pretreatment could improve the Pickering emulsion stability by altering the structure of IRBPPP.

title: Computational epitope engineering of flurodifen and haptens for ultrasensitive immunoassay development
abstract: Flurodifen (Flu), a widely used but potentially hazardous herbicide, demands a rapid and efficient detection method for real-time monitoring to mitigate health risks. In this study, the electrostatic characteristics of haptens and Flu were systematically analyzed using a computer-aided technology. High-performance Flu monoclonal antibody (mAb) 2A4 (IC 50 = 0.62 ng/mL) was successfully prepared based on anti-mechanism interference effects. The visual detection limit (vLOD) of colloidal gold immunochromatographic test strip (CGIA) to detect Flu for cucumber, cabbage, wheat, and corn samples were 5, 5, 10, and 10 ng/g. Recovery rate was 90.0-98.0 %, and the coefficient of variation (CV) was 1.39-9.43 %. Validation results of positive samples detected by LC-MS/MS method established in this study demonstrated the high accuracy of the CGIA method, it provided visual detection results within 15-20 min, offering an efficient tool to implement timely interventions and mitigate the effects of pollution events.

title: Decoding bitter peptides in soy sauce: From identification to mechanism in bitter taste formation
abstract: The molecular basis of bitterness in soy sauce was investigated through an integrated approach combining peptidomics, sensory evaluation, cell biology, and molecular docking. Ethanol-extracted bitter peptides (BPs) were identified via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Seventeen BP candidates were shortlisted based on toxicity, allergenicity, bitterness predictions and hydrophobicity calculation. Sensory evaluation showed that 13 peptides exhibited bitterness, with 8 significantly enhancing bitterness of 6 key free amino acids in soy sauce. Using a HEK-293T cell-based cAMP assay, FYL and VLY were identified as hTAS2R4 ligands (EC₅₀ = 62.11 and 199.51 μM, respectively). Molecular docking revealed that both peptides bind primarily via hydrophobic interactions to residues such as VAL85, PHE88, and PHE62. These findings provide a theoretical basis for bitterness mechanism and flavor improvement of soy sauce.

title: Mechanisms of partial replacement of table salt with potassium and calcium salts on yolk gel formation in salted duck eggs
abstract: The trend towards low-salt pickling is crucial for the health-conscious evolution of the salted egg industry. This study investigated the potential of potassium chloride (KCl) and calcium chloride (CaCl 2 ) as substitutes for sodium chloride (NaCl) in salted egg pickling, focusing on microstructural changes and protein interactions during yolk gel development. Results indicated significant improvements in β-sheet content and gel stability in the KCl and NaCl (Na + K) group. KCl enhanced the compactness and hardness of the egg yolk gel, reducing sodium content by 46.28 % while improving protein-lipid interactions. Conversely, the gel formation rate in the CaCl 2 and NaCl (Na + Ca) group decreased, reducing sodium content by 63.88 %. Overall, the inclusion of KCl and CaCl 2 did not alter the gelation trend of egg yolks but modified the gelation process. These systems modulating gel formation through electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and hydrophobic, enriching the understanding of yolk gel formation with non‑sodium salts.

title: Astaxanthin-rich Haematococcus pluvialis mitigates oxidative damage and restores gel functionality in myofibrillar protein for enhanced meat product quality
abstract: Oxidative degradation of myofibrillar protein (MP) in meat products compromises texture and functionality, necessitating effective natural antioxidants. This study investigated the effects of Haematococcus pluvialis (HP) supplementation on structural properties and thermal gelation capacity of oxidized MP. HP, an astaxanthin-rich microalga, mitigated oxidative damage and enhanced gel formation under oxidative stress. Results demonstrated that 1.0 % HP addition reduced protein carbonyl content by 43.1 % and increased sulfhydryl content by 17.3 %, indicating significant inhibition of oxidative modifications. HP also elevated MP surface hydrophobicity by 44.6 % and induced secondary structural shifts. HP optimized gel properties, strengthening gel networks (31.7 % increase in hardness) and improving water-holding capacity by 14.0 %. Dynamic rheological tests showed increased storage modulus (G') and loss modulus (G"), signifying enhanced elasticity and viscosity. SEM analysis showed HP promoted denser, uniformly structured gel matrices. Collectively, HP emerges as a promising next-generation antioxidant for meat systems, effectively restoring functional attributes of oxidized MP.

title: Inactivation of polyphenol oxidase and peroxidase in whole wheat flour using atmospheric cold plasma treatment: Kinetics, mechanism, and impact on its compositional properties
abstract: This study examines polyphenol oxidase (PPO) and peroxidase (POD) inactivation in whole wheat flour (WWF) using atmospheric cold plasma (5-25 kV/1-10 min) and steam treatment (100 °C/1-6 min) while assessing the changes in enzyme structure. Cold plasma at 25 kV/10 min and steam at 100 °C/6 min achieved ≥99 % inactivation of PPO and POD. The inactivation followed nth-order kinetics, with orders of 1.15 for PPO and 1.1 for POD under cold plasma exposure. PPO was more resistant than POD in WWF. Both treatments increased random coil content, confirming enzyme unfolding. Increasing plasma exposure led to higher optical emission intensities of reactive nitrogen species (328-426 nm), hydroxyl radicals (314 nm), and oxygen molecular bands (739 and 778 nm). Cold plasma at 25 kV/10 min preserved the color and proximate composition of WWF. These findings highlight cold plasma's potential as a non-thermal alternative for PPO and POD inactivation while maintaining WWF's compositional integrity.

title: Implementation of transglutaminase 2 as a crosslinking agent for salivary oral models: Effects in (in)soluble complexes formation and compound adsorption with different polyphenol families
abstract: Astringency, a trigeminal sensation common in polyphenol-rich foods, involves two mechanisms: salivary protein precipitation (M1) and polyphenol adsorption onto mucosal or epithelial surfaces (M2). This study investigates the role of transglutaminase 2 (TGM2) in enhancing mucosal pellicle formation and influencing these mechanisms. Oral cell-based models were optimized using three TGM2 titers and two incubation times, identifying 0.2 U.mL-1 as optimal for significantly increasing cross-linked proline-rich proteins, statherin, and P-B peptide. Optimized models were exposed to tannic acid (TA, hydrolysable tannins) and grape seed extract (GSE, condensed tannins). In whole saliva (WS) models, M1 was the dominant interaction, particularly for TA (74–83%) versus GSE (40–44%). In saliva-free conditions, TA showed stronger adsorption (M2), with up to a 12.8-fold increase over M1. GSE exhibited minimal M2 interaction. These results highlight how astringency mechanisms differ by compound and oral environment, offering a refined model for studying molecular interactions and sensory effects of polyphenols.

title: Effect of soy protein isolates obtained by weak-base synchronized membrane separation on nanoemulsion stability: A comparison with alkaline extraction/isoelectric precipitation and salt extraction
abstract: Efficient extraction of soy protein isolate (SPI) with high functionalities from soybean meal is essential for developing stable emulsion formulations. This study compared the effects of three extraction methods on protein yield and the stability of nanoemulsions prepared by the obtained soy protein isolate (SPI). We found that the protein recovery of the weak-base synchronized membrane separation (MS) extraction (53 %) was much higher than that of alkali extraction/isoelectric point precipitation (AE, 38 %) and salt extraction (SE, 27 %). During the storage stage (15 days at 55 °C), MS-SPI-stabilized nanoemulsions showed better physicochemical stability (e.g. particle size ∼285 nm, turbiscan stability index∼4.1) than AE-SPI- and SE-SPI-stabilized nanoemulsions, and comparable stability to commercial sodium caseinate. This was further verified by cryo-SEM/TEM, as MS-SPI had more tightly and uniformly distributed particles at the oil-water interface, facilitating the formation of a solid-like interfacial film. Therefore, MS-SPI is a highly stable emulsifier for developing nanoemulsion-based food.

title: Ultrasound-assisted egg yolk granule–EGCG conjugation via multiple mechanisms for improved functionality and stability
abstract: This study explores ultrasound-assisted egg yolk granules (EYG)-EGCG conjugation via non-covalent (NC), acidic (C3), alkaline (C9), and free-radical (FR) mechanisms. All methods achieved high-binding efficiency (62-68 %). C9 exhibited the smallest particle size (112 nm), most uniform distribution (PDI 0.25), highest ζ-potential (-40 mV), and lowest surface hydrophobicity (78.4 %), resulting in outstanding protein solubility (95 %) and exceptional emulsifying performance (EAI: 24.0 m 2 /g; ESI: 770 min) through structural unfolding and electrostatic stabilization. While FR and NC exhibited the highest antioxidant inhibition ratios (DPPH: 77-80 %; ABTS: 71-87 %; FRAP: 80-83 %), C9 uniquely balanced functionality, with creaming stability (100 % for 5 h) and tiny, uniform emulsion droplets (0.5-2 μm). Spectroscopic and thermal analyses confirmed that alkaline conditions best modulate protein structure and stability. In contrast, NC, C3, and FR induced aggregation or oxidative crosslinking, compromising functionality. C9 conjugation is recommended for functional food and nutraceutical applications requiring stability and emulsification.

title: Specific enrichment of antioxidant peptides from tilapia skin enzymatic hydrolysate by methyl methacrylate modified MCM-41
abstract: Peptides derived from aquatic by-products exhibit excellent functional properties. This study aimed to enrich tilapia skin peptides (TSP) with antioxidant activity, using the mesoporous material MCM-41 modified with methyl methacrylate (MMA), a hydrophobic monomer. Herein, the poly-MMA (PMMA)-MCM-41 was synthesized and used to enrich the antioxidant properties of enzymatic hydrolysate-derived TSP. Additionally, a pseudo-second-order adsorption kinetics model was utilized to verify the adsorption behavior of PMMA-MCM-41 toward TSP. Thermodynamic analysis revealed that the adsorption of TSP on PMMA-MCM-41 was similar to the Freundlich model. PMMA-10 exhibited an adsorption capacity of 171.73 mg/g, with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC 50 ) for scavenging the radicals of 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH·), 2,2'-azino-bis (3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS + ·), and hydroxyl (·OH) in the enriched peptides being 0.068 ± 0.007, 0.178 ± 0.005, and 0.039 ± 0.004 mg/mL, respectively. Notably, the antioxidant activity of the peptide significantly improved compared with that of the original peptide TSP. The specific enrichment of antioxidant TSP by PMMA-10 was primarily accomplished through size-exclusion chromatography and hydrophobic interactions. Altogether, the findings of this study show the great potential of PMMA-modified mesoporous materials in enriching functional peptides derived from aquatic by-products.

title: Mushroom β-glucans as immunomodulators: Elucidation of structure-function relationship
abstract: Mushrooms are the fruiting bodies of fungi and are recognized as abundant sources of essential nutrients and bioactive molecules. β-Glucans are naturally occurring fungal cell wall polysaccharides identified as non-toxic modulators of the immune system, making them ideal candidates for natural immunotherapy, and a promising dietary intervention through their application as a functional food. Notably, there is a vast structural diversity among β-glucans isolated from various fungal species, resulting in differences in their immunomodulatory activities. This structural heterogeneity has led to the unsolved question – which β-glucan/s have the most potent biological and/or immunological properties. While there is extensive literature on the structure and function of mushroom β-glucans, their structure-function relationships remain unclear. In this report we will consolidate the insights related to the diversity of mushroom β-glucan structure and immunomodulatory activity with specific emphasis on structure-function relationships, as well as the effect of extraction and purification techniques on β-glucan structure and immune activity. • β-Glucans are naturally occurring non-toxic modulator of the human immune system. • Structural diversity of β-glucans affects their immunomodulatory function. • Understanding the β-glucan structure-function relationship will broaden their applications. • Knowledge on the effect of extraction and purification techniques on β-glucan structure is critical for maximizing their therapeutic potential.

title: A dual reversible-mode near-infrared AIE fluorescent probe: naked-eye identification and removal of CN− and HSO3−/SO32− anions from food and environmental samples
abstract: We report a novel near-infrared AIE fluorescence probe TPA-S-Cy3. Fluorescence spectra showed that TPA-S-Cy3 specifically recognized CN - with a detection limit of 122.00 nM. In terms of UV colourimetric discrimination, both HSO 3 - /SO 3 2- and CN - anions could discolour TPA-S-Cy3, with HSO 3 - /SO 3 2- fading better and the detection limit for HSO 3 - /SO 3 2- was found to be 791.00 nM. Meanwhile, the HSO 3 - /SO 3 2- complex can produce hydroxyl radical oxidative addition under UV irradiation, and this restores the TPA-S-Cy3 structure and colour. TPA-S-Cy3 upon complexation with CN - do not undergo this change, and thus HSO 3 - /SO 3 2- and CN - can be identified by simple UV irradiation with the 'naked eye'. In view of the low detection limits of TPA-S-Cy3 for HSO 3 - /SO 3 2- and CN - anions, the spiked recoveries of TPA-S-Cy3 for both environmental and food testing were in accordance with the requirements. In addition, the detection of SO 2 and HCN gases was achieved by loading TPA-S-Cy3 onto a hydrogel.

title: A low-cost in situ nanoparticle coating with high encapsulation efficiency and continuous release capability for inhibiting flesh lignification and enhancing antioxidant capacity and cold tolerance of loquat fruit
abstract: Loquat fruit is vulnerable to postharvest chilling lignification. Fumigation with methyl jasmonate (MeJA) could inhibit the lignification, but is inefficient. The present study developed nanoparticles encapsulated with MeJA (MeJA@NPs) with high encapsulation efficiency (94.83 %) and 30 d sustained release capability. Then, a transparent, edible, in situ coating was prepared by blending a gelatin/pullulan solution with MeJA@NPs. The coating could continuously inhibit chilling lignification of loquat fruit, where the firmness increase and lignin accumulation were reduced by 82.7 % and 52.3 % respectively after 6 d of storage. Further analysis of the inhibition mechanism showed that the coating suppressed the peroxidase activity, thereby blocking lignin polymerization. Besides, the coating could also enhance the antioxidant capacity of fruits via activating cinnamate 4-hydroxylase and 4-coumarate: CoA ligase and upregulating the superoxide dismutase, catalase, and ascorbate peroxidase activities. In conclusion, our work provides a novel approach of in situ nanoparticle coating on fruits for postharvest preservation.

title: Bioinspired chitosan coatings enhanced with bacterial cellulose nanocrystals and apple polyphenols for preservation of perishable fruits
abstract: This study presents a multifunctional chitosan-based composite coating integrating bacterial cellulose nanocrystals (BCNC-I, derived via sulfuric acid hydrolysis) and apple pomace polyphenols (AP) to prolong perishable fruit shelf life. The optimal formulation (4 % BCNC-I + 0.25 % AP) exhibited enhanced mechanical strength (61.5 % increase) and barrier performance (45.7 % reduction in water vapor permeability) compared to pure chitosan, alongside robust antioxidant efficacy (71.7 % DPPH and 78.4 % ABTS radical inhibition). When applied to fig (Ficus carica L.) fruits, the coating significantly suppressed respiration rate (50.1 % reduction) and weight loss (47.9 % decrease) during 15-day storage (4 °C, 85 %RH), while preserving firmness, titratable acidity, total phenolics, and total flavonoids at levels comparable to freshly harvested fruit. The complementary roles of BCNC-I-providing structural reinforcement and AP-contributing antioxidant activity collectively establish a sustainable, dual-functional coating system that helps reduce dependence on synthetic packaging. This study highlights the potential of biopolymer-based composites in tackling postharvest losses and advancing eco-conscious food preservation strategies.

title: Recent advances in SERS hotspot regulatory strategies and their applications in food safety detection
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) offering molecular specificity and rapid detection capabilities. However, its practical applications in food safety detection face limitations including low sensitivity in complex food matrices, nanostructure instability, inconsistent signal reproducibility from uneven hotspots, and poor analyte-substrate affinity. To address these challenges, strategic modulation of SERS hotspots, nanoscale regions with amplified electromagnetic fields, has become imperative. This review highlights tailoring nanoparticle morphology, optimizing surface chemistry, integrating synergistic materials, and advancing fabrication to create substrates with tunable enhancement and improved stability. These advancements enable precise detection of diverse food contaminants, including pesticide residues, illegal additives, biotoxins, and pathogens, at ultralow concentrations. Remaining challenges include scalable manufacturing, cost-effective materials, and real-world matrix compatibility. Addressing these limitations through innovative hotspot modulation will unlock SERS's full potential as a cornerstone technology for on-site, high-throughput food safety monitoring, ensuring rapid and precise identification of contaminants to safeguard public health.

title: Determination of 71 pesticides in huajiao using an improved multiplug filtration cleanup method with UHPLC-Q-TOF/MS
abstract: This study established an improved multiplug filtration cleanup method coupled to UHPLC-Q-TOF/MS for high-throughput detection of 71 common pesticide residues in fresh green huajiao, dried green huajiao, and dried red huajiao. The method only requires a 30 s gravity filtration to complete the purification of a single sample. Samples were extracted using acetonitrile containing 1 % formic acid, and graphitized carbon black, octadecyl silica, and primary secondary amine were used as cleaning agents. The method showed strong correlation (R 2 ≥ 0.99), acceptable recovery (70.2 %-119.8 %), and great repeatability in the three different huajiao matrices. In addition, it demonstrated good sensitivity, with limits of detection for the 71 pesticides ranging 0.0001-0.025 mg/kg for fresh green huajiao and 0.0001-0.03 mg/kg for dried green/red huajiao. Results indicated that this analytical method is an effective approach for both high-throughput screening and reliable quantitative detection of multiple pesticide residues in complex food matrices.

title: Accurate quantification of small bioactive peptides derived from dairy and plant-based beverages using isotope-coded dimethyl labeling and LC-MS/MS
abstract: Small bioactive peptides found naturally in foods or released during processing or gastrointestinal digestion can exert important biological activity, but their effectiveness depends on concentration, bioaccessibility, and bioavailability. Yet, accurate quantification of these peptides in complex food matrices and digesta remains limited. This study presents a cost-effective method for quantifying small peptides using isotope-coded dimethyl labeling with LC-QqQ MS in multiple reaction monitoring mode. The method was optimized across dairy and non-dairy beverages and validated with soy beverage digesta, selected for its significant protein level. Validation showed high accuracy (91.1–106.0 %), low intra-day precision (≤5.0 %), and inter-day instrumental precision (≤7.3 %) for 24 di- and tripeptides, with LOD and LOQ at sub-ppb levels for most analytes. The method was applied to bovine milk, soy, and almond beverages and their digesta, revealing dynamic peptide levels during digestion. This approach may be extended to quantify peptides in other complex food and biological matrices. • Stable isotope-coded dimethyl labeling enables isotopologue internal standard use. • Validation data confirmed high accuracy and precision for peptide measurement. • Specific bioactive peptides in dairy and plant-based drinks were quantified. • Bioactive peptide levels and trends varied by beverage type and digestion stage.

title: Functionalized nanofiber-based efficient sorbent for simultaneous extraction of multiple mycotoxins and its molecular dynamics simulation
abstract: Mycotoxins pose significant threats to public health and the economy. In this study, a novel functionalized nanofiber membrane was fabricated through electrospinning of polystyrene/polyacrylonitrile blended with carbon nanopowder and dopamine self-polymerization (PDA@PS/PAN-CNP NFM). The PDA@PS/PAN-CNP NFM was utilized as a nanofiber-packed solid-phase extraction (PFSPE) adsorbent, exhibiting brilliant extraction performance for multiple mycotoxins. Coupled with high-performance liquid chromatography equipped with a fluorescence detector (HPLC-FLD), a sensitive and rapid method for detecting trace mycotoxins in corn, bamboo shoots, sorghum, and their derivatives was developed. Under optimized conditions, the method showed good linearity, recovery (91.84 %-99.12 %), precision (RSD < 6 %), and low limits of detection (0.06-4.46 μg/kg). Notably, each extraction column could be reused for 25 cycles. Moreover, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed the interaction mechanisms between mycotoxins and the adsorbent, providing molecular-level insights into the adsorption dynamics. The results demonstrate great potential for application in the simultaneous determination of multiple mycotoxins.

title: Fabrication of Rubus chingii Hu ellagitannins-loaded W/O/W double emulsion gels stabilized by WPI/pectin complexes: Physicochemical properties, digestion characteristics, and transformation of ellagitannins
abstract: Ellagitannins (ETs) exhibit beneficial effects on gut microbiota modulation and bioactivity, but their instability compromises the delivery efficiency and absorption. Therefore, a double emulsion gel (DEG@RETs) loading with Rubus chingii Hu ETs (RETs) was constructed and optimized to enhance its gastrointestinal digestion stability and intestinal transformation. The optimal DEG@RETs formulation was 4 % pectin, calcium-induced gelation, W 1 /O: W 2 of 4: 6, and W 1 : O of 5: 5. Which achieved an encapsulation efficiency (EE) of 88.68 ± 4.36 %, maintained spherical structures with an EE (78.57 ± 1.34 %) after digestion. The DEG@RETs demonstrated pH and freeze-thaw stability while EE declined after heating at 90 °C. Cryo-SEM confirmed a crosslinked gel network. In vitro fermentation, transformation efficiency demonstrated significantly enhanced with urolithin A, urolithin B and ellagic acid increased by 7.37-, 3.19- and 7.87-fold respectively. These results proved that DEG@RETs can be an effective strategy to improve the colon-targeted delivery and biotransformation efficiency of RETs.

title: First identification of 1-hydroxyoctan-3-one in apple purees: Use as a fruit quality segmentation marker and correlation with octane-1,3-diol concentration
abstract: An organoleptic defect described as musty and/or fresh mushroom can occur in cooked apple products. GC-Olfactometry was used to characterize puree spoilage associated with sensory descriptors mushroom, cellar-like, musty, dusty or metallic. This approach, coupled with pure standards analysis allowed us to identify for the first time 1-hydroxyoctan-3-one in spoiled matrices. Using a targeted approach, 1-hydroxyoctan-3-one and octane-1,3-diol, were quantified by Stable Isotope Dilution Assay LC-MS/MS. Quantification results attested that these compounds exhibited a higher concentration in spoiled purees than in control ones and could thus be relevant markers of fruit spoilage. In a second time, the origin of 1-hydroxyoctan-3-one and octane-1,3-diol was investigated by contaminating several apple purees with specific fungal species. A Penicillium digitatum strain appeared to be the highest 1-hydroxyoctan-3-one producer, while a Botrytis cinerea strain led to a decrease of octane-1,3-diol concentration in spoiled products. It opens up avenues for the quality segmentation of fruits.

title: Exploiting wheat flour maturation for noodle quality improvement: The role of protein cross-linking and flour properties
abstract: This study elucidates the dynamic relationship between gluten protein evolution during wheat flour maturation and noodle quality modulation. Maturation for 40-50 days induced progressive increases in gluten index, Glutenin/Gliadin ratio, and glutenin macropolymer (GMP) content, with temperature-dependent amplification of these effects. Moisture distribution analysis further confirmed that 40 °C enhanced gluten-water interactions. Noodles made from flour matured at 25 °C for 40 days showed significant quality improvements, with cooking loss and soup turbidity decreased from 5.41 % and 34.75 % to 4.54 % and 30.55 %, respectively. At 25 °C, optimal protein cross-linking improved noodle extensibility, while 40 °C induced excessive cross-linking and lipid oxidation, reducing color stability and palatability. Conversely, the effect of the 15 °C condition was relatively limited. Overall, wheat flour matured at 25 °C for 40-50 days promoted moderate protein cross-linking, optimizing the color stability and processing performance of noodles.

title: Chlorpyrifos detection in strawberry and soil samples using a direct Z-scheme heterojunction photoelectrochemical sensor based on Bi2WO6 nanosheets loaded with MOFs-derived In2O3 hollow nanotubes
abstract: Chlorpyrifos (CPF) is widely utilized in agricultural practices, and its residue in food raise significant concerns food safety. However, current detection methods often suffer from complex operation procedures and unstable signal responses. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a reliable sensor for detecting CPF residue in food samples. In this work, a Z-scheme heterojunction was formed using hollow In 2 O 3 (H-In 2 O 3 ) and Bi 2 WO 6 nanosheets. The staggered band structure of the H-In 2 O 3 /Bi 2 WO 6 heterojunction facilitates carrier separation and transfer, thereby enhancing the sensor's response. In the presence of CPF, it reacts with ·OH radicals generated by the heterojunction, further amplifying the signal. The sensor exhibits a linear response in the range of 5-700 nM with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.72 nM. In addition, this photoelectrochemical sensor demonstrates satisfactory stability, anti-interference, selectivity and reproducibility, showing great potential for CPF analysis in real samples.

title: From morphology to metabolites: Integrated analysis of chemical and functional diversity in six shape-distinct premium green teas
abstract: Premium green tea is a general term for a class of unique and distinctive green teas with different shape. Non-targeted and targeted metabolomics analysis based on liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry combined with bioassays are used to study the quality characteristics of six premium green teas with different shapes, namely Longjing, Biluochun, Huangshanmaofeng, Yuhuacha, Yongxihuoqing and Xinyangmaojian. A total of 63 marker compounds were identified, including catechins, flavone glycosides, phenolic acids, and hydrolysable tannins. Energy spectrum analysis showed the elemental composition of tea, including major elements such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and trace elements such as selenium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium. Furthermore, bioactivity profiling revealed six green teas possess strong antioxidant properties, with Longjing excelling in antioxidants, Biluochun in acetylcholinesterase inhibition, Huangshanmaofeng in α-glucosidase/α-amylase suppression. This study establishes a foundation for precision modulation of green tea quality through shape-specific processing to optimize functional components aligned with consumer demands.

title: Dealcoholization of wine by vacuum distillation: Volatile and non-volatile profile, and sensory analysis
abstract: This study produced partially (PDW) and fully dealcoholized (DW) white, rosé, and red wines via vacuum distillation (VD), analyzing ethanol removal impacts on physicochemical, color, and volatile profiles, alongside sensory attributes. Ethanol reduction significantly increased density, total extract, glycerin, total acidity, and volatile acidity, while decreasing pH. Color shifts (ΔE ≥ 3) were perceptible in DW wines, with red DW exhibiting the highest ΔE (24.33). Total aroma compounds declined progressively (72–80 % loss in PDW; 89–94 % in DW). Sensory evaluation highlighted reductions in fresh floral (white/rosé), fresh fruity (red), sweetness (white/rosé), hotness, and body/fullness (rosé), while color intensity (red), cooked vegetable notes, and acidity (white/rosé) increased after ethanol removal. PDW and DW white/red wines retained original overall acceptability scores, whereas rosé acceptability decreased. Overall, VD efficiently produced DW adhering to regulatory alcohol limits, offering insights into ethanol removal's impact on wine properties, essential for optimizing dealcoholized product quality. • Vacuum distillation efficiently produces partially (PDW) & dealcoholized wine (DW). • DW shows higher A420nm, color intensity, and significant color difference (ΔE*). • Production of DW results in volatile compound losses up to 94 %. • PDW and DW white/red wines maintain overall acceptability; rosé wines scored lower.

title: Inhibitory effects of polysaccharides of various sources on 2-amino-3,8-dimethylimidazole[4,5-f] quinoxaline (MeIQx) in roasted beef patties
abstract: In this study, the effects of various sources polysaccharides, including chitosan, hawthorn polysaccharide and lentinan, on MeIQx (2-amino-3,8-dimethylimidazole[4,5-f] quinoxaline) formation in roasted beef patties were investigated. Results showed that hawthorn polysaccharide had the strongest inhibitory effect, while only chitosan decreased free MeIQx in a dose-dependent manner. For bound MeIQx, the inhibitory effect of chitosan, hawthorn polysaccharide, and lentinan were 14 %, 22 %, and 39 % at 0.1 % addition. When increased to 0.5 %, the inhibition rate was 26 %, 40 %, and 36 %. None of the polysaccharides increased the inhibition rate of MeIQx at 1 % addition (25 %, 36 %, and 33 %, respectively). Overall, the MeIQx content may be related to the polysaccharides themselves have excellent water retention capability. Additionally, polysaccharides effectively eliminated the intermediates. The carbonyl content and TBARS were reduced due to the free radical scavenging activity of polysaccharides. This study provides a theoretical basis for the polysaccharides to reduce MeIQx in high-temperature meat processing.

title: Structural and morphological optimization of low-salt myofibrillar proteins aggregates by ultrasound treatment: modulation of thermal aggregation behavior
abstract: Excessive sodium intake increases cardiovascular risks, driving demand for low-sodium meat products. Yet low-salt conditions (0.2 M NaCl) weaken the solubility and gelation capacity of pork myofibrillar proteins (MPs). This study investigated the mechanism by which ultrasound treatment (500 W, 20 kHz, 60 % amplitude) modulated the thermal aggregation behavior of low-salt pork MPs to enhance their gel properties. Changes in the secondary and tertiary structures of the modified MPs, along with their thermal aggregation behavior, were systematically characterized and comprehensively analyzed. Results showed that ultrasound treatment (500 W, 20 kHz, 60 % amplitude) significantly (p -5 mol/g and elevated surface hydrophobicity to 81.49 %, thereby suppressing aggregate nucleation. At 50 °C, ordered aggregates formed through hydrophobic domains. Subsequently, at 80 °C, the gel network transitioned from a predominantly salt-bridge structure to one stabilized by covalent bonds, as confirmed by scanning electron microscopy. This approach provides an efficient strategy for developing low-salt pork products (e.g., sausages, hams) and facilitates the industrial production of healthier meat alternatives.

title: Insight on nicotine insecticides in Guizhou Province, China: Residue analysis and risk assessment in different types of agricultural products
abstract: NIs have become prevalent contaminants. Given the limited understanding of residual profiles and toxicological impacts of NIs in different food, assessing their health risks are crucial. This investigation analyze 813 samples of different types from Guizhou Province. Key factors of spatiotemporal distribution patterns, dietary risk of eight NIs were quantified. Acetamiprid, imidacloprid, thiacloprid, thiamethoxam and clothianidin were mainly detected in plant-derived commodities, whereas not have NIs in meat. IMI RPF is correlated with the annual average temperature, the number of tourists, and the amount of pesticide usage. The risk assessment results indicate that although the acute risk associated with NIs residues in these foods is significantly higher than the chronic risk, these risks are acceptable.
