In contrast, the ternary conjugate (S-M-G) combined both advantages, maintaining high solubility (53.4 % at pH 7) and reducing surface hydrophobicity by 14.4 % compared with SPI. Emulsions stabilized by S-M-G showed the highest ESI (1434.7 min) and no creaming after five months of storage. These results indicate that ternary Maillard conjugation overcomes the intrinsic limitations of SPI and offers a promising strategy for developing stable natural protein emulsifiers.

title: Physicochemical characteristics of decolorized zein-based composite films and their utilization in developing dual-channel pH-responsive labels incorporating carbon dots and anthocyanins
abstract: This study developed a dual-channel pH indicator utilizing hydrophobin to enhance the compromised structural integrity of bio-based pH indicator films affected by moisture, while also addressing the limitations in pH response sensitivity and stability associated with single-mode detection. This indicator facilitates stable and real-time pH monitoring under daylight and ultraviolet illumination, incorporating zein with anthocyanins and carbon dots. To reduce interference from the inherent coloration of zein on colorimetric performance, activated carbon was utilized for decolorization, and the adsorption kinetics, along with optimal operational conditions, were systematically examined. The findings demonstrated that decolorization attained equilibrium after 5 h at 55 °C. Composite film analysis experiments revealed that the incorporation of anthocyanin and carbon dots improved matrix compatibility through hydrogen bonding interactions, leading to a denser microstructure and thereby enhancing the thermal stability and water insolubility of the composite film. The label demonstrated a sensitive and distinct dual-channel response, with color difference (ΔE > 5) across various pH conditions, confirming excellent color response capability. This study effectively developed a zein-based intelligent indicator label, exhibiting high sensitivity and reliability in detecting pH variations, indicating significant potential for monitoring the spoilage of perishable foods such as seafood and dairy products.

title: Exploring the regulation mechanism of digestibility of starch-polyphenol-protein ternary system by pH from multiple perspectives
abstract: This study investigated pH-dependent modulation of starch digestibility in rice starch-quercetin-whey protein isolate system (RS-QUE-WPI). Results showed that the WPI-QUE binding affinity, starch-polyphenol interactions, and QUE degradation kinetics at different pH values collectively affected starch digestibility. Acidic conditions (pH 3) promoted hydrogen bond interactions between molecules and decreased WPI-QUE binding affinity, enhancing structural ordering in RS-QUE-WPI (R 1047/1022 = 1.109, RC = 23.49 %). This structural change improved thermal stability, and viscoelasticity of RS-QUE-WPI while reducing solubility and swelling power, ultimately lowering starch digestibility and increasing resistant starch content (49.25 %). In contrast, alkaline conditions (pH 9) strengthened the interaction between QUE and WPI, accelerated QUE degradation, and disrupted the structural ordering of RS-QUE-WPI, which collectively increased starch hydrolysis rates and decreased resistant starch content. Findings elucidate the mechanism of pH-driven modulation of starch digestion in complex food matrices, providing a potential strategy for designing functional foods with controlled glycemic response.

title: Selenium-enriched tea - chemical composition and health benefits
abstract: Selenium-enriched tea has attracted increasing attention for its potential health benefits, arising from the synergistic effects of selenium and tea-derived compounds. Tea plants are capable of absorbing exogenous selenium applied through soil fertilization or foliar spraying, and efficiently converting its inorganic forms into more bioavailable organic compounds. Such enrichment not only enhances the levels of beneficial constituents in tea (e.g., polyphenols, catechins, amino acids, polysaccharides, caffeine) but also contributes to improved flavour and aroma. The chemical composition of a Se-enriched tea infusion is influenced by multiple factors, including soil selenium levels, fortification methods, leaf processing techniques, and brewing conditions (e.g., temperature, steeping time, and the water-to-leaf ratio). Owing to the complexity of these parameters, the literature contains some contradictory findings. Nevertheless, studies on the health benefits of Se-enriched tea suggest positive effects on antioxidation, anti-inflammation, hepatoprotection, intestinal protection, and anticancer activity. This brief overview summarizes recent advances in research on selenium-enriched tea and discusses the impact of selenium accumulation on tea composition as well as its significance for human nutrition and health.

title: Smartphone-integrated chameleon ratiometric lanthanide MOF sensor: Semi-quantitative fluorescence for real-time biomarker discrimination in complex environment and foods
abstract: Developing fast and convenient sensors for 2,6-dipicolinic acid (DPA) is of great importance for enhancing microbiological safety in food and healthcare, with significant implications for broader industrial applications. This work presents lanthanide metal-organic frameworks ([Ln(H 2 atiip) 2 (phen) 2 (H 2 O) 5 (MeOH)] n , Ln = Eu, Tb), named as CUST-865 and CUST-866. This is the first time that principal component analysis method is utilized to distinguish DPA. DPA molecules precisely replace the coordinated water molecules in the metal-organic framework, enabling the construction of an open ratiometric lanthanide fluorescent sensor. Furthermore, a novel "one-to-two" logic sensor with a single-input and dual-output configuration was developed. This system exhibits chameleon-like behavior, dynamically adapting its output signals in response to the input. Furthermore, smartphone platforms equipped with color recognizer applications enable detection of DPA. The detection limits for CUST-865 and CUST-866 were determined to be 0.19 μM and 1.15 μM in tap water, and 0.22 μM and 1.11 μM in milk powder.

title: Development of 3D printed chocolate with reduced saturated fat using starch-based oleogels
abstract: Developing 3D printed chocolate with reduced saturated fat is challenge yet vital for chocolate production. Current study fabricated 3D printed chocolate with reduced saturated fat by partially replacing cocoa butter (10 %, 25 %, 50 %, and 75 %) with different starch-based oleogels. Composition and ratio of oleogels used altered the physicochemical properties of resulting reduced saturated fat chocolates. Thermal analysis indicated that substituting 10 % to 75 % of cocoa butter by oleogels led to significant decreases in melting peak temperature and enthalpy of cocoa butter, but retained two endothermic peaks of chocolate and polymorphic form V of cocoa butter. Rheological measurements revealed that reduced saturated fat chocolates exhibited declined apparent viscosity but similar shear-thinning behavior and gel structure to chocolate. Despite significant decrease in hardness, reduced saturated fat chocolates with up to 75 % cocoa butter being replaced displayed good printability. This work provides a novel approach to improve printability and health aspect of chocolate.

title: Mineral oil contamination along the cocoa supply chain: impact of storage and transportation in jute bags and assessment of contamination transfer into cocoa powder and cocoa butter
abstract: On-line high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) – gas chromatography (GC) analysis of 28 whole cocoa beans before and after transport in jute bags contaminated with mineral oil hydrocarbons (MOH) showed that average saturated hydrocarbons (MOSH) increased from 0.9 to 9.6 mg/kg, with aromatic hydrocarbons (MOAH) reaching 2.3 mg/kg. On average 40% of the MOH migrated into whole beans reached the shelled beans, with a cut-off at n-C25. Post-transport jute bags contained diverse mixtures of MOH, varying in both amount and molecular weight distribution, as well as MOAH percentage. It was estimated that MOAH n-C10-25 exceeding 220 mg/kg in new jute bags expose whole beans to contamination above 2 mg/kg. GC×GC coupled to single quadrupole mass spectrometry (MS) proved effective for detailed MOH characterization. Throughout the supply chain, MOH contamination was transferred to cocoa mass, sometimes influenced by external lubricant inputs, and partitioned into cocoa butter and powder according to fat content.

title: Multi-perspective investigation of the effects and interaction mechanisms of three common dietary fiber on cassava starch properties
abstract: This study investigates the effects and interaction mechanisms of three common dietary fibers-cellulose (CE), hemicellulose (HE), and lignin (LI)-with cassava starch (CS). Results indicate that all three dietary fibers interact with CS through hydrogen bonding and other non-covalent forces, with binding capacities ranked as HE > LI > CE. Distinct binding modes are observed: CS is wound around CE single chains to form locally specific circular windings; CS and HE are intertwined to form double-helix-like structures; and CS wraps around LI to form V-type complexes. Differences in binding capacities and binding modes result in distinct effects of the three dietary fibers on starch properties, with their influence ranked as LI > HE > CE in reducing viscosity and enhancing thermal stability. However, in reducing digestibility, the order shifts to HE > LI > CE, with the highest HE addition yielding the lowest glycemic index (64.96 ± 0.35 %).

title: Artificial neural network-assisted colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode aptasensor for the detection of β-conglycinin
abstract: β-Conglycinin is the most important allergen in soy, and accurate detection of it is of great significance for ensuring food safety. In this study, a novel multifunctional bio-inspired nanozyme Au@His-MIL-88 was used as a signal probe to construct an artificial neural network (ANN) model-assisted colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode aptasensor by combining with catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA). The detection range of this method was 5-5000 ng/mL with a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.31 ng/mL. The recovery of β-conglycinin in real samples exhibited a range of 93.1-114.0 %, indicating its practicality. The integration of aptamers and CHA expanded the scope of target applications and improved detection sensitivity. Additionally, the ANN model can achieve deep integration and mutual correction of dual-mode sensing signals, thereby reducing regression errors and improving detection efficiency. The developed detection method has broad application prospects in the field of food allergen detection.

title: Modulation of phenolic compounds in murta (Ugni molinae Turcz) juice by lactic fermentation in monoculture and coculture: identification and quantification of extractable and non-extractable fractions by HPLC-QTOF-MS
abstract: Controlled lactic acid fermentation may be a strategy for valorization of plant matrices such as murta ( Ugni molinae Turcz), a Chilean berry rich in phenolic compounds. This study evaluated the effect of fermentation in monoculture with Lactobacillus acidophilus and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum , as well as in coculture, under two optimized conditions (SAW and GDF) on the content, structural profile, and antioxidant capacity of extractable (EP) and hydrolysable (HP) polyphenols in murta juice. High Performance Liquid Chromatography coupled to Quadrupole Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry (HPLC-QTOF-MS) analysis identified 59 EP compounds, including methylated and glycosylated derivatives not previously reported in murta, evidencing a fermentation-induced structural reconfiguration. Additionally, 13 compounds (not present in unfermented samples) were identified in the hydrolysable polyphenol fraction, demonstrating the contribution of this constituent to a comprehensive assessment of the murta phenolic profile. The results showed significant increases in extractable polyphenols and their antioxidant activity (FRAP and ABTS) in GDF conditions, highlighting the coculture (323 ± 18 mg/100 g dw) as the most effective. These findings confirm that using optimized fermentative conditions, particularly in coculture, not only increases the concentration and diversity of phenolic compounds but also underscores the importance of integrating extractable and hydrolysable polyphenol fractions to broaden the utilization of murta juice in developing fermented beverages with enhanced functional properties. • Murta juice fermentation modified extractable and non-extractable phenolic compounds. • The phenolic profiles changed after lactic fermentation of murta juice. • New methylated, glycosylated, and acylated phenolics emerged after fermentation. • Cocultures exhibited superior capability to biotransform phenolic compounds.

title: Complexation of chitosan-modified porous starch with chlorogenic acid to form ternary gels: Multiscale structural changes and retrogradation behavior
abstract: Various food additives can delay starch retrogradation, but research on their mechanisms affecting the multiscale structure and retrogradation behavior of starch gels is lacking. This work introduces porous starch (PS), chitosan (CTS), and chlorogenic acid (CA) and modulates their interactions to develop a ternary gel system with reduced retrogradation and enhanced storage stability. Porous chitosan-modified starch (PS-CTS) with a stable multi-layered structure was prepared, achieving 68 % CA adsorption and minimizing its thermal degradation. A PS-CTS-CA ternary gel with strong hydrogen bonding was constructed through thermal induction, showing a uniform and dense porous network structure, low long- and short-range orders, and high viscoelasticity and water retention. CTS and CA synergistically inhibited starch chain alignment, reducing water migration and retrogradation degree (Rd, with Rd 28 decreasing by 35 % at 28 days) during storage, improving storage stability significantly. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the development of stable and high-performance starch-based gel foods.

title: A ternary AuNP/NiFe-LDH/MWCNT heterostructure enhanced electrochemical biomimetic sensor for sensitive detection of enrofloxacin in aquatic foods
abstract: The development of sensitive and selective electrochemical sensors for antibiotic detection is critical to ensuring food safety. Herein, we report a novel biomimetic electrochemical sensor using a ternary AuNP/NiFe-LDH/MWCNT heterostructure combined with molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) for detecting enrofloxacin (ENR) in food. The AuNP/NiFe-LDH/MWCNT composite was prepared by in-situ reducing HAuCl 4 on a NiFe-LDH/MWCNT backbone, forming a heterojunction structure that enhances charge separation and electron transfer. Electropolymerization of pyrrole with ENR produced highly selective MIP layers. The synergistic integration of high conductivity, abundant catalytic sites, and selective molecular recognition endows the sensor with excellent electrochemical performance. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range (0.05-100.0 μM) and an ultralow limit of detection (LOD) 0.025 μM. It showed superior selectivity, reproducibility, stability, and applicability in complex aquatic food samples, with recoveries of 94.6 % to 103.9 %. This work paves the way for practical, high-precision monitoring of trace antibiotics in food safety applications.

title: Multidimensional quality assessment (nutrients and aroma) of dried kiwifruit: Unveiling the advantages of radio frequency-vacuum drying
abstract: Dehydration is an effective method for reducing postharvest losses of fresh kiwifruit, yet comprehensive comparisons of conventional and emerging drying techniques on multidimensional quality attributes remain limited. The effects of radio frequency-vacuum drying (RFVD), hot air assisted radio frequency drying (HARFD), hot air drying (HAD), and heat pump drying (HPD) on physicochemical properties, texture, nutrients, functional characteristics, and flavor profiles of dried kiwifruit were systematically evaluated. Results showed that HARFD had the shortest drying time (6.5 h). In comparison, HPD showed the longest time (9.5 h) but achieved the highest sugar-acid ratio (1.38 ± 0.15), total polyphenols (4.53 ± 0.08 mg GAE/g), vitamin C (0.92 ± 0.04 mg/g), and antioxidant capacity. RFVD samples had the highest content of flavonoid (7.94 ± 0.06 mg RE/g) and ester volatiles (9.7 %), along with superior texture, microstructure, and sensory qualities. Overall, RFVD was considered an effective method for producing high-quality, ready-to-eat dried kiwifruit snacks.

title: Sustainable ultrasound-assisted extraction of xanthones from mangosteen pericarp using deep eutectic solvents: mechanism insights and efficiency analysis
abstract: Mangosteen (Garcinia mangotana L.) pericarps, comprising about two-thirds of the fruit, is often discarded, causing resource waste and environmental impact. Studies show it is rich in bioactive compounds xanthones and holds significant potential for applications. This study developed a DES-UAE method and identified choline chloride/1,2-butanediol (1:5; 30 % (v/v) water) as optimal. Through single-factor and response surface methodology (solid-liquid ratio 1:110 g/mL, temperature 45 °C, time 55 min (360 W, 25 kHz)), xanthones yield reached 56.76 ± 0.65 mg/g DW, an 22.0 % improvement over conventional methods. Molecular dynamics revealed that DES forms more and stable hydrogen-bond networks with xanthones (lifetime 3.93 ps), with shorter bond lengths, smaller supplementary angles, and lower interaction energy (-344.80 kJ/mol), enhancing stability and diffusion. This study demonstrates that DES-UAE efficiently increases xanthones yield while remaining highly recyclable, with the extraction performance of the DES decreased by only 7.04 % after three reuse cycles.

title: Differential accumulation of triterpenoids in Ziziphus jujuba and Ziziphus acidojujuba: insights from terpenoid metabolomics across organs and developmental stages
abstract: Triterpenoids constitute the principal bioactive compounds in jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) and sour jujube (Ziziphus acidojujuba Cheng et Liu), but their spatiotemporal distribution and metabolic accumulation patterns remain understudied. In this work, metabolomic analysis via UPLC-MS/MS identified 85 distinct triterpenoid metabolites, comprising 57 triterpenes and 28 triterpene saponins. Triterpenes accumulate mainly in the root bark and branch bark, whereas triterpenoid saponins are concentrated mainly in the flowers and young/mature leaves. In the prefruit stage, triterpene saponins accumulate, whereas in the later stages of development, triterpenes metabolites subsequently accumulate. Quantitative analysis revealed that betulinic acid had the highest concentration in the root bark (4.945 mg/g). This study provides the first comprehensive, metabolomics characterization of triterpenoid composition and accumulation dynamics in jujube and sour jujube and may guide future applications in functional food development and phytopharmaceutical research.

title: Ultrasonic-assisted preparation of resistant starch: advances in methods, structural properties, functional characteristics, and applications
abstract: Resistant starch (RS) is increasingly valued in functional foods for its prebiotic benefits and role in chronic disease prevention. Ultrasound-assisted preparation has emerged as a sustainable method to enhance RS functionality and digestive resistance. However, comprehensive understanding of its preparation, properties, and applications remains limited. This review explored ultrasound-assisted RS production, focusing on structural modifications, physicochemical properties, and food applications. Studies showed that ultrasound, when combined with heat, enzymes, or chemical treatments, boosted RS content via three key mechanisms: (1) increasing amylose and molecular rearrangement, (2) promoting double-helix formation, and (3) creating ordered composites. Ultrasonic cavitation modified starch granule structure, enhancing enzyme resistance through steric hindrance. Physicochemical traits (solubility, pasting, rheology, thermal stability) depended on ultrasound settings, starch type, and preparation methods. Potential applications include low-glycemic-index foods, baked goods, and emulsion stabilizers, highlighting ultrasound's promise for sustainable RS production. Future work should refine industrial-scale ultrasound processes and investigate health impacts.

title: Comparative effects of enzymatic hydrolysis by four proteases on the structure, functional properties, and bioactivities of lactoferrin
abstract: This study investigated the effects of Alcalase, ficin, trypsin, and papain on the structure, function, and bioactivities of lactoferrin (LF). The results demonstrated that LF was hydrolyzed by all four proteases, with Alcalase being most effective. Treatment with the four proteases modified the particle size distribution of LF, resulting in a decrease in large particles and generation of abundant low-molecular-weight fragments. Treatments with four proteases increased the free amino acid content. These enzymatic treatments reduced the α-helix structure of LF while enhancing intrinsic fluorescence and reducing extrinsic fluorescence, indicating modifications in secondary and tertiary structures. Ficin hydrolysate exhibited the strongest foaming capacity, foaming stability and fat absorption capacity, whereas papain hydrolysate demonstrated the highest emulsifying activity index. Notably, Alcalase hydrolysate displayed superior DPPH radical scavenging activity, Fe 2+ chelating activity and Caco-2 cell inhibitory activity. This study provides a theoretical foundation and scientific evidence for modifying LF through enzymatic hydrolysis.

title: L-cysteine-mediated disulfide bond modulation enhances gelation behavior of ginkgo seed protein/hyaluronic acid gels
abstract: This study explores the influence of sulfhydryl/disulfide bond exchange reaction on the physicochemical properties of ginkgo seed protein isolate (GSPI)/hyaluronic acid (HA) gels. The disulfide bond content in the gel was modulated by incorporating varying concentrations 5 mmol L -1 N-ethylmaleimide (NEM) and 1-50 mmol L -1 L-cysteine (L-Cys). Results indicated that NEM inhibited disulfide cross-linking, thereby resulting in a weak gel network. Conversely, the addition of L-Cys effectively regulated disulfide bond formation. Specifically, 5 mmol L -1 L-Cys promoted the generation of additional disulfide linkages, contributing to a more compact and refined gel structure with improved textural characteristics. However, higher L-Cys concentrations (> 25 mmol L -1 ) reduced disulfide bond content and weakened the gel structure. These findings demonstrate that the characteristics of GSPI/HA gels can be effectively tailored by modulating their disulfide bond content. L-Cys, therefore holds potential for enhancing the gelation behavior of GSPI, expanding its applicability in gel-based food products.

title: Corrigendum to “Effects of varying proportions of grape skins, seeds, and stems added pre-fermentation on tannin and anthocyanin evolution in Marselan wine” [Food Chem. 493 (2025) 145628]
Ginger as a novel starch resource: Preparation, structural characterization and physicochemical properties
abstract: This study systematically investigated the structural characteristics and physicochemical properties of ginger starch, comparing them with those of corn starch (CS). The results revealed that ginger starch granules exhibited elongated oval and round-like shapes, with a smooth and flat surface, birefringence, an A-type crystalline structure, and a smaller particle size than CS. Compared to CS, ginger starch had higher amylose (31.16 ± 0.39 %) and post-cooking resistant starch content (15.54 ± 0.58 %), longer average chain length of amylopectin, and higher crystallinity (24.83 %). However, its weight-average molecular weight, radius of gyration, degree of branching, and short-range ordered structure were lower than those of CS. In terms of functional properties, ginger starch demonstrated excellent thermal stability and shear processing tolerance, though its overall functional properties remained inferior to CS. Notably, ginger starch had significantly higher total phenolic content, exhibiting greater antioxidant activity. These findings provide insights for developing new starch resources and advancing ginger processing and utilization.

title: Cili pomace-enhanced chitosan/cellulose nanofibril composite films for antioxidant, antibacterial, and biodegradable food packaging
abstract: Cili (Rosa roxburghii Tratt.) pomace is rich in bioactive components, making it a promising additive for functional packaging materials. Cili pomace extracts (CLPE) were incorporated into chitosan/cellulose nanofibril (CS/CNF) matrices to develop a food packaging material-strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding among CS, CNF, and CLPE, leading to amorphous structural features. The CS/CNF/CLPE composite films, particularly those with 20 % CLPE loading, displayed significantly reduced water vapour permeability (WVP), enhanced thermal stability, and superior UV-blocking capacity. Additionally, the enrichment of CLPE endowed the composite films with potent functional properties, enhancing their antibacterial efficacy against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. In strawberry preservation tests, the CS/CNF/20 %CLPE film solution inhibited decay, minimised weight loss, and maintained fruit quality. Additionally, films containing CLPE accelerated biodegradation, with over 70 % degradation occurring within 21 d. Therefore, the multifunctional CS/CNF/CLPE composite film, which leverages the valorisation of agricultural by-products, presents a promising sustainable packaging candidate for active food preservation.

title: The rise of molecularly imprinted polymers in food analysis: selective, reliable, and cost-effective approaches
abstract: Molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs), commonly known as "artificial" or "plastic" antibodies, serve as synthetic substitutes for natural receptors. Over the past five decades, MIPs have garnered significant interest in both academic research and commercial sectors, spanning diverse fields from medicine to food. The analysis of food presents a formidable challenge due to the intricate nature of food matrices and the minimal concentration of analytes. However, molecular imprinting techniques, with their exceptional selectivity and sensitivity, are perfectly equipped to address these two obstacles. Moreover, MIP methodologies remain highly favored owing to their myriad advantageous attributes, such as ensuring food safety, maintaining quality, enabling traceability, and facilitating detection. This article sheds light on innovative perspectives regarding the applications and advancements of molecular imprinting technology within the food industry, alongside MIP-based analytical methods and prospective future applications.

title: Germinating under magnetic field improved nutrient composition, physicochemical properties and flavor of mung bean
abstract: Germination enhances the nutrient composition of grain, but the effects of germinating under magnetic field (MF) on physicochemical properties and flavor of mung bean have been poorly understood. In this study, mung beans germinated under MF were evaluated by assessing germination index, nutrient composition, physicochemical characteristics and flavor. Compared with 72 h without MF, the germination rate was elevated by 13.0 % after 72 h of MF. The reducing sugar content rose by 10.7 %, the γ-aminobutyric acid content increased by 74.9 %, and the polyphenol content grew by 50.2 %. MF also improved physicochemical properties of mung bean, including solubility and swelling power. Moreover, MF enhanced the flavor profile. These findings demonstrated that MF has significant potential for application in the development of functional grain-based foods.

title: A computationally driven screening-construction-mechanism strategy of magnetic molecularly imprinted polymers for aliphatic aldehydes detection
abstract: Sensitive detection of aliphatic aldehydes in food is hindered by excess derivatization reagents. In this study, a computationally driven screening-construction-mechanism strategy is proposed to enrich aldehyde derivatives while mitigating the adverse effects of excess derivatization reagents. Density functional theory was employed to optimize 20 functional monomers, seven solvents, and three cross-linkers, followed by tuning template/monomer ratios and Fe 2+ dosage to synthesize magnetic molecularly imprinted polymers MMIPs-APBA under the optimal parameters. As magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE) adsorbents, MMIPs-APBA achieved rapid equilibrium (10 s), high selectivity for aldehyde derivatives (imprinting factor of 6.2), and minimal adsorption toward derivatization reagents (imprinting factor of 0.025), blocking over 90 % interference signals. Finally, the adsorption mechanism of aldehyde derivatives by MMIPs-APBA is elucidated by three wave function analysis methods. The developed method, combining MMIPs-APBA-based MSPE with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, is successfully applied for the rapid and accurate determination of eight aliphatic aldehyde derivatives in food samples.

title: Storage life prediction and quality discrimination of instant green tea: Integrating computer vision, electronic nose, and electronic tongue
abstract: Tea storage is a critical determinant in determining the quality of tea products. This study systematically investigated the quality alterations of instant green tea during storage and developed an intelligent evaluation method by integrating computer vision, electronic nose, and electronic tongue with machine learning. Quantitative chemical profiling established statistically significant correlations between conventional quality indicators and multi-sensor intelligent features. Machine learning models effectively classified the storage duration of instant green tea, with the electronic tongue achieving a classification accuracy exceeding 98 % for storage time prediction. Furthermore, data fusion combined with feature selection algorithms enhanced the predictive accuracy for both storage duration and key quality content. The integration of intelligent sensing technologies provides a robust methodology for rapid shelf-life prediction and quality discrimination of instant tea, establishing a scientific foundation for quality control and authenticity assurance in the tea industry.

title: 11,12-dihydrolactaroviolin from edible mushroom Lactarius hatsudake Tanaka as a selective inhibitor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
abstract: Identifying functional food factors is crucial for food research. In particular, edible mushrooms contain natural antibacterial compounds, which can be used to develop functional foods. In this study, we isolated 11,12-dihydrolactaroviolin (dihydro-LAC), an antibacterial compound, from Lactarius hatsudake Tanaka (L. hatsudake), which selectively inhibited Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis), including 80 drug-resistant strains, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 7.8 μg/mL. 500 μg/mL of dihydro-LAC showed no significant cytotoxicity to normal cells and enhanced the streptomycin clearance of M. tuberculosis. The results of molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations showed that dihydro-LAC targets CmaA2 and MmaA2 enzymes in M. tuberculosis to interrupt cell wall synthesis. Further transcription and expression explorations validated the downregulation of the predicted targets. Furthermore, substrate accumulation occurred in mycolic acid biosynthesis in targeted metabonomics. This work offers valuable insights into the functional factors of edible mushrooms and provides a new functional food resource for specific populations.

title: Effects of chlorine dioxide oxidation on the structure and gel functionality of crayfish myofibrillar protein
abstract: This study systematically investigated the concentration-dependent effects of chlorine dioxide (ClO 2 , 0-150 mg/L) on the structural and gelation properties of crayfish myofibrillar protein. The results demonstrated that ClO 2 decomposition generated hydroxyl radicals (•OH) in a concentration-dependent manner, thereby inducing induced progressive protein oxidation. As the ClO 2 concentration increased, a significant increase was observed in carbonyl content, dimeric tyrosine formation, and surface hydrophobicity, concomitant with a decrease in sulfhydryl groups, free amino groups, and protein solubility. Secondary structure analysis revealed a shift from α-helix to β-sheet and random coil. Moderate oxidation (<100 mg/L) enhanced gel strength through disulfide cross-linking., whereas concentrations exceeding 100 mg/L induced severe oxidation (e.g., methionine oxidation and cysteine trioxidation), resulting in coarse, disordered protein aggregation, significantly compromising gel water-holding capacity. Thus, 100 mg/L is recommended as the optimal threshold to balance disinfection efficacy and protein functionality in crayfish processing.

title: Sonication and sodium alginate synergistically modify whey protein emulsion gels for enhanced delivery of astaxanthin bioaccessibility
abstract: Astaxanthin's immense health benefits are hampered by its chemical instability and poor bioaccessibility. Conventional whey protein concentrate (WPC) carriers offer limited protection. The study aimed to develop a superior delivery system by constructing a WPC-based emulsion gel synergistically modified with sodium alginate (SA) and ultrasound. The combined treatment (0.75 % for SA, 200 W for ultrasonic power, 40 °C for ultrasonic temperature and 20 min for ultrasonic time) yielded a robust carrier with high encapsulation efficiency (over 90 %) and water-holding capacity (96.5 ± 1.02 %), achieving an astaxanthin retention of 80.96 ± 0.24 % and a bioaccessibility of 60.15 ± 0.96 %, which significantly surpasses that of conventional WPC systems. The primary advantage of this strategy lies in the synergistic creation of a denser gel network, which enhances physical stability and provides superior protection during digestion. These findings demonstrate the high potential of this SA-sonication strategy for developing high-performance bioactive delivery systems in functional foods and nutraceuticals.

title: Enzymatic synthesis of medium-and long-chain triacylglycerols (MLCTs): Bridging triacylglycerols compositional gaps between infant formulas and human milk
abstract: Medium-and long-chain triacylglycerols (MLCTs) are critical components of human milk fat, playing a critical role in infant fat absorption and growth. This study compared MLCT compositions between human milk and commercial infant formulas, revealing that human milk is rich in MLL-type (containing one medium-chain fatty acid and two long-chain fatty acids) MLCTs, whereas all formulas showed distinct triacylglycerol profiles, with significantly lower MLL content. To address this gap, an enzymatic synthesis method was developed for human milk fat substitutes (HMFS) using blended oil and lauric acid as substrates. Under optimized conditions (lauric acid:oil = 3:1, 50 °C, 8 % Lipozyme RM, 3 h), the process yielded 80.98 % MLCTs and 48.13 % MLL, with major species (e.g., 18:1/12:0/12:0, 18:2/12:0/12:0, 18:1/16:0/12:0, 18:1/18:2/12:0) closely matching human milk. The resulting HMFS also exhibited a lower melting point and reduced thermal degradation compared to unesterified oils. This study provides a promising approach for developing HMFS for infant formula.

title: A dual-photoelectrode self-powered photoelectrochemical aptasensor based on metallophthalocyanine-sensitized photoanode amplification coupled with core-shell SiO2@Tb-MOF quenching
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) poses severe threats to human health even at trace levels, necessitating the development of rapid and sensitive detection methods. This work presents an innovative self-powered photoelectrochemical aptasensor for ultrasensitive AFB1 monitoring. Specifically, zinc phthalocyanine-sensitized MgIn 2 S 4 as a high-performance photoanode, where the sensitization narrows bandgap and extends light absorption, generating enhanced photocurrent for biological detection. Furthermore, Au@CuGaO 2 as a stable photocathode that provides abundant biomolecule binding sites while circumventing the false-positive issues inherent in conventional anodic sensing platforms. Notably, SiO 2 @Tb-MOF as a dual-function quencher that simultaneously competes for visible light excitation and creates steric hindrance to block electron donor access, achieving significant signal amplification. The synergistic effects of these components yield exceptional analytical performance, including an ultra-wide linear range (0.01 pg/mL to 100 ng/mL) and a low detection limit (0.0032 pg/mL). The satisfactory anti-interference, reproducibility and stability provide a solid foundation for the application of this sensing platform.

title: Dynamic variation of bioactive compounds and techno-functional components of dough fortified with wheatgrass powder during steaming process
abstract: This study explored the feasibility of wheatgrass powder (WGP) as a functional additive in dough by examining bioactive compound dynamics and structural changes in gluten and starch during steamed bread production. Folates and chlorophyll levels declined during steaming due to thermal degradation, with 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-CH 3 -THF) and chlorophyll b being more heat-sensitive, although 5 % WGP formulation retained the highest levels throughout the processing. Thermodynamic and rheological analyses demonstrated that WGP reduced starch gelatinization and significantly decreased the elastic (G') and viscous (G") moduli of the dough, indicating a weakened gluten network. β-sheet/β-turn structures increased at the expense of α-helix of gluten proteins with WGP (especially 5 % WGP reduced α-helix content by approximately ∼10.9 %). The step-wise reduction of disulfide (SS) bonds indicated that WGP impeded gluten polymerization by weakening the strength of SS bonds. Microstructural analysis confirmed a fragmented gluten matrix and exposed starch granules especially 5 % WGP addition. Volatile substances analysis identified notable aroma modifications with WGP addition, characterized by elevated esters and terpenes. The results demonstrate the ability of WGP as a bioactive fortificant, though optimized processing is needed to preserve bioactive integrity and product quality.

title: Effects of sun drying combined with baking processes on the flavor quality of Chongqing Tuocha raw tea
abstract: The quality of Chongqing Tuocha raw tea (CTRT) processed by different drying methods was analyzed. The results showed that baked then sun-dried (BS) groups sensory score were higher than sun-dried then baked (SB) groups. With baking time increasing, amino acids levels increased, flavonoid glycosides levels decreased. Umami and sweet amino acids levels in BS3 group (38.65 and 37.65 mg/g) were 3.27 % and 5.80 % higher than in the BS1 group. Flavonoid glycoside levels were lowest in the BS3 and BS2 (782.92 and 731.49 nmol/g). Argininosuccinic acid, N,N-dimethylglycine, isosilybin, 7,4'-dihydroxyflavone and scutellarin were tightly correlated to bitterness, L-glutamic acid and trans-4-hydroxy-l-proline were closely related to umami. Volatile components content in the BS2 group (62.36 μg/g) was 15.42 % higher than in the SB1 group. Twenty key volatile substances were screened. 1-nonen-3-one, β-Ionone, non-8-enal and trans-beta-ionone were the main aroma contributors for each group. Thus, BS3 and BS2 were favorable to improve CTRT quality.

title: Corrigendum to “Probabilistic health risk assessment of rare earth elements through rice (Oryza sativa L.) consumption using Monte Carlo simulation” [Food Chem. 496 (2025) 146760]
Non-destructive assessment of bayberry quality using hyperspectral imaging analysis: from individual to template-packaged product via model transfer
abstract: Bayberries are soft and delicious fruits, yet their quality grading poses significant challenges. This study presents hyperspectral imaging (HSI) analyses for predicting weight and soluble solids content (SSC) of bayberries in individual and those stored in template-packages, sourced from three batches collected from different regions and dates. A simple image process was to measure bayberry quality using image regional descriptors and average grayscale spectra. Bayberry weight was predicted using multiple linear regression, achieving a root mean squared error of prediction (RMSEP) of less than 0.6. SSC prediction utilized an optimized competitive weighted resampling algorithm combined with partial least square (PLS), resulting in an RMSEP of less than 0.8. To enhance prediction accuracy for other batches individual or packaged bayberries, a slope-bias correction (SBC) method was employed to transfer the PLS model. SBC effectively addressed prediction deviations across different batches and acquisition modes, demonstrating its potential for enhancing HSI-based quality assessment.

title: Influence mechanism of fixation on the development of green tea flavor and related non-volatile and volatile metabolites by objective quantification, widely targeted metabolomics, and aroma metabolomics
abstract: Fixation is key for green tea flavor formation; however, the impact of fixation methods on non-volatile metabolites (NVMs) and volatile metabolites (VMs) regulation remains unclear. We applied objective quantification techniques, widely targeted metabolomics, and aroma-omics to analyze the influence of fixation methods on green tea quality. Roller-hot air coupling fixation (RHF) produced an umami taste with a chestnut aroma, whereas roller-steam coupling fixation (RSF) produced a tender aroma with bitterness. We detected 498 NVMs and 63 VMs, and 14 key quality-differential NVMs and 7 key VMs were identified. KEGG revealed flavonoid, amino acid, glycoside, and carotenoid metabolism were the key pathways caused by fixation methods resulting in green tea flavor difference. RHF accelerated flavonoid transformation and amino acid formation metabolism, resulting in higher L-glutamic acid and catechin contents, lower rutin and l-lysine contents. These results provide a theoretical and technical support for precise targeted processing of high-quality green tea.

title: Effects of polar quercetin and non-polar resveratrol on the functional properties, oxidative stability and interfacial behavior of camellia oil body emulsions
abstract: This study investigated the effects of quercetin and resveratrol on the functional properties, oxidative stability, and interfacial behavior of camellia oil body emulsions. Polyphenols were incorporated individually and in combination to examine their interactions with interfacial proteins and the lipid phase. Quercetin preferentially interacted with OB surface proteins via hydrogen bonding, lowering interfacial tension from 18 to 14 mN/m and increasing hydrophobicity, while resveratrol mainly stabilized the lipid phase. Their combination significantly enhanced the thermal stability, interfacial protein concentration, and droplet stability, as confirmed by Turbiscan analysis. Polyphenol incorporation markedly suppressed lipid oxidation, reducing PV from 60 ± 4 to 22 ± 2 meq/kg and improving DPPH and ABTS radical scavenging capacities up to 70 %, with OB-QR showing the highest antioxidant performance. FTIR revealed protein conformational changes, and decreased sulfhydryl and amino groups indicated polyphenol-protein interactions. Overall, polarity-driven partitioning enabled dual-phase stabilization, offering a clean-label strategy for OB-based formulations.

title: Multivalent Cu sites in CuFe2O4@Cu@C synergistically enhance electrochemical detection and degradation efficiency of organophosphorus pesticides
abstract: Pesticides are omnipresent environmental pollutants negatively influencing on human health and ecosystem, emphasizing the urgent need for high-efficiency detection and degradation treatment measures. Herein, we propose an electrochemical detection and catalytic degradation dual system based on a multivalent Cu-based catalyst (CuFe 2 O 4 @Cu@C) that utilizes Cu-FcDA MOF as a sacrificial template. Experimental results suggested that enhanced detection and degradation efficiency originates from synergistic effect of multivalent Cu sites, that can significantly promote electron transfer and enrich active reaction sites, simultaneously favoring the enzymatic reaction and catalytic degradation reaction. Under optimal conditions, the established sensing method possesses satisfactory linear ranges (methamidophos: 7.4 × 10 -12 - 7.4 × 10 -7 M, and monocrotophos: 4.48 × 10 -13 - 4.48 × 10 -8 M), low limit of detection (methamidophos: 6.6 × 10 -14 M and monocrotophos:1.32 × 10 -14 M) and high recoveries (91.8 % ∼ 113.1 %). Meanwhile, the CuFe 2 O 4 @Cu@C(450)/PMS degradation system achieves nearly 100 % removal efficiencies towards multiple pesticides within 20 min. This study provides a reliable technology for simultaneously detecting and removing of hazardous organic contaminants, guarding the environmental and food safety.

title: Structural modification of ferulic acid for manipulating its bitterness inhibition regulation
abstract: This study identified 9 derivatives of ferulic acid via in silico screening, aiming to explore the effect of molecular structure on bitterness inhibition. Their HepG2 cell LC50 values ranged from 0 to 1.65 mg/mL.The electronic tongue test results indicate that [3-(3-nitro-4,5-dihydroxyphenyl) acrylic acid] and [3-(2-chloro-4-fluorophenyl) acrylic acid] improved Acesulfame potassium bitterness inhibition by 21.18-27.35 %. [2-oxo-3-phenylpropionic acid] and [4-phenylbut-3-enoic acid] enhanced coffee bitterness suppression by 38.31-42.09 %. The absence of CC bonds in ferulic acid reduced inhibition, while nitro/phenol groups boosted suppression. Ferulic acid and its derivatives were found to form hydrogen bonds with residues R268 and Y241 in the TAS2R46 bitterness receptor, as identified by docking experiments (in silico), a critical condition for the bitterness suppression activity. These findings provide new insights for the development of bitterness inhibitors in the future.

title: Dissipation dynamics, processing factors and risk assessment of 26 pesticides and their metabolites in strawberry from field to table
abstract: Through field trials, this study investigated the dissipation, metabolism, processing factors (PFs), and risk assessment of 26 pesticides and their metabolites from field to table. The half-lives of 25 pesticides detected in strawberries ranged from 1.3 to 4.8 days, following first-order dissipation kinetics. During cooking, the concentrations of most pesticide residues increased (PF = 1.13-2.44). Freeze-drying significantly increased residue levels for nearly all pesticides (PF = 4.01-30.02), except for pymetrozine. In contrast, soaking was found to effectively reduce the concentrations of most pesticide residues (PF = 0.04-0.84). Chronic and acute dietary risk assessments conducted across various countries and populations indicate that the health risks associated with the consumption of fresh strawberries, strawberry crisps, and strawberry jam are within acceptable limits. This study provides valuable data for controlling pesticide residues in processed products, offering significant theoretical and practical implications for ensuring the quality and safety of strawberries.

title: Edible coatings from plant-derived natural gums: a review of food industry applications
abstract: This review critically evaluates recent advances (2018-2025) in the development and application of plant-derived natural gums as edible coatings and film for food preservation. Natural gums such as guar gum, locust bean gum, and karaya gum exhibit excellent film-forming properties and barrier characteristics, protecting against moisture, oxygen, and microbial contamination. These biodegradable polymers are compatible with diverse food matrices, maintaining product quality and extending shelf-life. They reduce post-harvest losses in fresh produce by 15-30 % while enhancing processed food stability through modified atmospheric conditions. Unlike earlier reviews, including Saha and Bhattacharya (2017), which focus primarily on the structural and film-forming characteristics of traditional gums such as guar, locust bean, karaya, and tragacanth, the present work emphasises new trends in gum modification (chemical, enzymatic, and nano-composite approaches) and emerging processing technologies such as electrospinning, layer-by-layer deposition, and cross-linking. It also integrates quantitative data and coating performance, reporting 15-40 % improvements in shelf-life and 30-60 % reductions in water vapour permeability through composite formulations. Furthermore, this review distinguishes itself by analysing industrial feasibility, scalability challenges, and sustainability implications for large-scale food applications. By focusing exclusively on natural gums, this article provides a gum-specific perspective distinct from broader edible coating reviews, offering a framework to guide future research and commercial translation of these biopolymers in sustainable food system. Additionally, their ability to carry bioactive compounds and antimicrobial agents support the development of functional foods with improved health benefits. The use of these renewable materials aligns with consumer demand for clean-label products and sustainable packaging solutions. The review also addressed current technological limitations and proposed future research directions to optimize the performance of gum-based coatings in various food applications.

title: Impact of oil unsaturation on crystalline particles and self-assembled fiber oleogels: Physicochemical properties, crystallinity, and potential mechanism
abstract: This study investigated how oil unsaturation affects the properties of crystalline particles (β-SIT+MG, βM) and self-assembled fiber (β-SIT+γ-ORY, βγ) oleogels (OG). Using olive oil (OO, C18:1), safflower oil (SO, C18:2), and linseed oil (LO, C18:3) as oil phases, three types of oleogels (OO OG, SO OG, LO OG) were prepared for βM/βγ series. In βM series, OO OG showed the highest hardness (425.85 g) and storage modulus (G': 3.58 × 10 4 Pa), while LO OG was weakest. In βγ series, LO OG exhibited superior gel strength (hardness: 2783.78 g, G': 3.51 × 10 5 Pa). XRD revealed that higher unsaturation disrupted βM crystal lamellae, lowering crystallinity. However, LO's higher mobility promoted aggregation and crystallinity in β-SIT and γ-ORY. FT-IR and molecular docking studies confirmed that unsaturated fatty acids exhibited higher interaction forces in βγ series, thereby enhancing gel strength. This study provides insights into oil unsaturation's impact on oleogels.

title: Ultrasensitive homogeneous electrochemiluminescence biosensor based on DNAzyme walker-regulated interface reaction rates strategy for one-step quantification of copper ions
abstract: Sensitive detection methods for trace heavy metal ions in complex samples are of great interest. Herein, a homogeneous electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor based on DNAzyme walker-mediated interface reaction rate regulation strategy has been developed for copper ions (Cu 2+ ). Ruthenium bipyridine-doped silica nanoparticles modified with Cu 2+ -activated DNAzyme (Cu-DNAzyme) and its substrate sequence (Cu-Sub) are designed as ECL nanoprobes. Negatively charged Cu-Subs on nanoprobes can effectively prevent ECL reaction of ruthenium bipyridine with coreactant and negatively charged electrode due to steric hindrance and electrostatic repulsion. When Cu 2+ ions exists, the Cu-DNAzyme walker is activated, cyclically cleaving Cu-Subs and thereby enhancing the ECL performance of nanoprobes, resulting in signal amplification. The biosensor enables sensitive Cu 2+ ions detection from 0.1 nM to 10 mM with a detection limit of 0.025 nM. Cu 2+ ions in real samples have been detected with satisfactory results, and it is promising for heavy metal ions detection in complex samples.

title: Effect of edible ethanol-induced redistribution of gluten proteins on fresh noodle quality and starch digestibility
abstract: This study explored how edible ethanol (0-5 %) affects fresh noodle quality and starch digestibility by examining its impact on gluten protein structure and redistribution. Ethanol treatment reduced dough mixing stability and extensibility, while increasing tensile resistance and stickiness. Microscopic structure images revealed ethanol-induced migration and redistribution of gluten/gliadin fractions. Chromatography showed partial solubilization and depolymerization of gliadin, enhancing its ability to coat starch granules. This led to increased starch enthalpy change (ΔH) and crystallinity, reducing starch digestion rates. Storage and thermal dehydration further promoted protein-starch interactions. Additionally, ethanol delayed browning and inhibited microbial growth, significantly extending noodle shelf life. Overall, ethanol treatment effectively reduces the starch digestion rate by altering the structure and distribution of gliadin proteins, offering a novel strategy for the development of fresh noodle products with a low glycemic index.

title: Coffee waste valorization: A comprehensive review of recent advancements and future directions for a circular bioeconomy
abstract: Spent coffee grounds (SCG) present both an environmental challenge and a significant nutritional opportunity. This comprehensive review of coffee waste valorization focuses on its transformation into safe, high-value ingredients within the food and nutritional sectors for a circular bioeconomy. Diverse SCG applications are detailed, focusing on the extraction and utilization of bioactive compounds (lipids, fiber, phenolics) for functional foods and nutraceuticals. Findings are critically synthesized, including the impact of compositional variability (species, roasting) on quality and the need for rigorous food safety assessments. These must address critical challenges like contaminant monitoring (mycotoxins, acrylamide) and regulatory compliance. Biotechnological strategies (mycoremediation, enzyme-assisted extraction) for enhancing nutritional value are also discussed. Future research prioritizes type-specific valorization, advancing green extraction (microwave, ultrasound assisted), and ensuring robust toxicological and long-term stability analyses for commercialization. This focused analysis confirms SCG's vital role in accelerating a sustainable, resource-efficient bioeconomy through innovation in food systems.

title: Deciphering microbial and metabolite dynamics in rice noodle fermentation: A metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic approach
abstract: Inoculated fermentation accelerates rice noodle production and improves quality, but the underlying microbe-metabolite dynamics remain unclear. This study employed metagenomic and non-targeted metabolomic profiling to investigate microbial succession and metabolic transformations during fermentation. Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus, Lactococcus cremoris, and Saccharomyces cerevisiae were identified as dominant strains, with Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus rapidly outcompeting other microbes and suppressing Klebsiella pneumoniae and Salmonella enterica by over 70 %. At 6 h, rice noodle hardness and springiness improved markedly, driven by microbial shifts and metabolic outputs. Metabolomic analysis identified 1405 metabolites, of which 57 showed significant changes: aspartic and citric acid levels declined by 14.99 % and 33.16 %, while citrulline, γ-aminobutyric acid, lactate, and Cinnamic acid increased by 16.38 %, 8.96 %, 70.69 %, and 63.90 %, respectively. Enzyme annotation indicated α-amylase and glycogen synthase regulate starch degradation and amylose synthesis. These findings provide insights into the microbial and metabolic mechanisms that enhance the quality of fermented rice noodles.

title: Spatio-temporal heterogeneity of quality attributes and flavors in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) cubes during deep frying: Key metabolic evidence
abstract: The study investigated the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of quality and flavor characteristics in grass carp cubes (GCC) during deep frying. Results revealed distinct layer-specific variations: the inner layer maintained the lowest fat content, A 280 (absorbance at 280 nm, intermediate Maillard reaction products), and A 420 (absorbance at 420 nm, advanced Maillard reaction products) values while exhibiting the highest moisture and protein content; the middle layer demonstrated the highest carbonyl value and volatile compound concentration (6821.36 μg/kg after 8 min of deep frying); whereas the outer layer showed the lowest peroxide value, protein and moisture content, coupled with the highest fat content and volatile compound diversity (50 species detected after 2 min of deep frying). Metabolomic analysis identified lipids, lipid-like molecules, organic acids, and derivatives as predominant differential metabolites. Additionally, eight KEGG pathways were identified as key metabolic pathways. The findings suggest that both Maillard reactions and lipid oxidation play pivotal roles in flavor development during GCC deep frying.

title: From hidden danger to rapid detection: silver-enhanced urchin-like tungsten oxide MEMS sensors for Listeria monocytogenes detection in refrigerated dairy
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes (LM), a foodborne pathogen renowned for its cold tolerance, often poses a contamination threat to dairy products, underscoring the urgent need for rapid detection methods to prevent outbreaks. Herein, urchin-like WO 3 nanostructures modified with Ag nanoparticles are employed to construct a highly active surface, which exhibits excellent sensing performance for 3-hydroxy-2-butanone (3H2B), a characteristic biomarker of LM. The 1.0 wt% Ag-WO 3 -based sensor characterized by high sensitivity (R a /R g = 92.7@30 ppm 3H2B), satisfactory repeatability, and potential for practical applications. Furthermore, confirmed that the chemical sensitization effect of Ag nanoparticles significantly reduces reaction activation energy. The developed gas sensor achieves highly accurate detection of LM at trace concentrations in dairy products. These insights could pave the way for the development of more efficient food safety diagnostics, ultimately contributing to enhanced public health protection.

title: A coumarin-benzothiazole probe-driven multimodal aptasensing platform for label-free analysis and portable visualization of kanamycin in milks
abstract: Kanamycin (KANA) is an aminoglycoside antibiotic that widely adopted in foods safety and the excessive intake can cause various symptoms. Although conventional methods for KANA detection have been well-developed, they still remain challenges in real scenarios application. We here report a coumarin-benzothiazole probe and KANA aptamer-based multimodal aptasensing platform (DR1/K-apt) to realize the efficient and accurate KANA analysis in milks. The formation of DR1/K-apt can severally produce the colorimetric/fluorescent/visual signals for KANA response within 30 min, which constitute the corresponded detection manners with sensitive detection limit (0.001 mM) and wide detection linear ranges. Especially, the fluorescence of DR1/K-apt can produce the obvious green-red-green colors variation and contribute to construct a smartphone-based portable paper device (K-cPAD) to reveal the facile quantification of KANA. It will hold the potential in realizing the large-scale instrument-free and chemical labelling-free KANA detection and offer a powerful tool in antibiotics evaluation and foods safety research.

title: Rational screening of anti-E. coli peptides via GAT-MD integration leveraging foodborne antimicrobial sequence features
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer promising alternatives to conventional antibiotics due to their broad-spectrum activity and multi-modal mechanisms. However, large-scale experimental screening remains costly and time-consuming. To expedite AMP discovery, this study proposes a combined screening strategy based on Graph Attention Networks and molecular dynamics simulations. Utilizing a food-derived bioactive peptide database, the method efficiently identified candidate AMPs with activity against Escherichia coli ATCC 25922 and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 33591 from a pool of 100,663,296 peptides. Experimental validation confirmed that the identified AMP, AMP_321, exhibited broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. The peptide demonstrated excellent stability and low hemolytic activity. Mechanistic studies revealed that AMP_321 exerts its antibacterial effect by disrupting bacterial membrane integrity, inducing extracellular ATP release, and promoting intracellular accumulation of reactive oxygen species. In food models, AMP_321 significantly reduced bacterial contamination on beef and tomato surfaces, validating its potential as a safe and effective natural food preservative.

title: The correlation of protein phosphorylation with protein degradation, oxidation, and endogenous enzyme activity in postmortem Esox lucius muscle
abstract: This investigation examined the correlation between phosphorylation levels of muscle proteins and textural characteristics, protein degradation, protein oxidation, and endogenous enzymatic activities in Esox lucius stored at 4 °C postmortem. Muscle quality gradually deteriorated during storage. Changes included a biphasic pH fluctuation (an initial decrease followed by an increase), increased myofibril fragmentation index (MFI), reduced shear force, elevated protein carbonyls, and diminished total sulfhydryl content. Endogenous proteases (μ-calpain, cathepsins B/L/D/H) remained active, and myofibrillar protein degradation occurred. As refrigeration time increased, phosphorylation of myofibrillar proteins (MP) gradually decreased, while phosphorylation of sarcoplasmic proteins (SP) increased. Correlation analysis showed that phosphorylation levels of MP and SP were significantly correlated with muscle texture, protein degradation, protein oxidation, and endogenous protease activity (P < 0.01 or P < 0.05). This suggests that protein phosphorylation may regulate postmortem changes in walleye muscle quality.

title: Editorial Board
Mung bean as an emerging source of starch: A review on its isolation, structure, functionality, modification, and application
abstract: Mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) is an edible legume seed which has attracted much attention due to its high carbohydrate and protein contents, as well as their bioactive components and potential health-promoting effects. Starch is the major component in mung bean (up to 41%), which can be used as an important bio-polymer in food and non-food industries due to its low price, biodegradability, renewability, storage stability, and availability. Mung bean starch (MBS) typically contains 16-45% amylose, giving it stronger gel-forming ability compared with many other starches. Its high resistant starch fraction (up to 80%) further highlights its promising potential for functional foods and low-glycemic applications. This review summarizes the current knowledge of the isolation, composition, chemical and granular structures, functional properties, and modifications of MBS, as well as its recent applications in biodegradable packaging, noodle production, and drug delivery systems as an emerging starch source.

title: Effect of lipid oxidation on the color deterioration of ready-to-eat oysters: Discussion based on the model system
abstract: The contribution of lipid oxidation to color deterioration in ready-to-eat (RTE) oysters remains unclear. Therefore, this study established four polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)-based model systems: P (PUFA), PG (PUFA + glucose), PA (PUFA + amino acids), and PAG (PUFA + amino acids + glucose). After accelerated storage (60 °C, 48 h), the browning index of the EPA- and DHA-added groups of the P system increased by 2.08- and 3.08-fold, respectively, indicating that lipid oxidation alone can cause browning. The browning extent followed P < PG < PA < PAG, indicating that glucose and amino acids independently and synergistically aggravated PUFA-induced discoloration. In PG and PA systems, glucose and amino acids enhanced coloration through radical-mediated reactions, respectively. The additional browning in the PA/PAG system was due to the formation of pyrrole and lipofuscin-like pigments. These results demonstrate lipid oxidation's key role in RTE seafood discoloration and provide a theoretical basis for quality control.

title: Evaluation and comparison of the nutritional quality of eggs of different goose breeds: Guidance for consumers and production
abstract: This study comprehensively evaluated the nutritional characteristics and market potential of six geographically indicated goose egg varieties: Magang, Kaijiang, Xingguo Grey, Wugang Copper, Yongkang Grey, and Laiyang Wulong. Among poultry eggs (chicken, duck, pigeon, and quail), goose eggs possess the largest weight, thickest shells, and highest yolk index, enhancing their durability for long-distance transport. Goose eggs contain high levels of monounsaturated fatty acids, calcium, selenium, zinc, high-quality protein and small-molecule functional substances, such as L-proline, N-acetyl-D-glucosamine, and pantothenic acid. The research emphasizes the need to explore quality variations among these varieties and analyze how origin environment, rearing system, feeds, and genetics effect these traits, providing a basis for breeding programs. Furthermore, it aims to offer reasonable dietary advice and product choices tailored to different consumer groups. Investigating these characteristics will support the development of higher-quality, value-added processed goose egg products.

title: Self-assembled peptides derived from sesame meal as novel carriers for β-carotene with enhanced bioavailability: A study integrating experimental and computational perspectives
abstract: This study aimed to develop a self-assembled nanodelivery system derived from sesame protein hydrolysates (SPH) for the efficient encapsulation and delivery of β-carotene (BC). SPH with a 12 % degree of hydrolysis (SPH DH12 ), prepared via alkaline protease-mediated hydrolysis, exhibited optimal self-assembly properties. Optimized parameters yielded 50.30 ± 0.43 nm BC-SPH DH12 nanoparticles with 75.23 ± 0.92 % encapsulation efficiency and 11.14 ± 0.14 % drug loading capacity. BC encapsulation triggered secondary structural shifts (33.8 % α-helix decrease, 41.9 % β-sheet increase) and masked characteristic FTIR peaks. Peptidomics integrated with coarse-grained molecular dynamics identified five core peptides for BC encapsulation via hydrophobic interaction-driven self-assembly. In vitro digestion showed BC-SPH DH12 effectively prolonged BC release (26.76 % cumulative release). Rat pharmacokinetic studies further confirmed superior absorption, with a peak plasma concentration of 64.98 ng/mL and 2.73-fold higher bioavailability versus free BC. This work confirms that SPH self-assembly represents an effective strategy for hydrophobic nutraceutical delivery.

title: Bioactivity-guided isolation of pancreatic lipase inhibitors from Lycium ruthenicum using a novel HPLC-FLD/pancreatic lipase online recognition system
abstract: The screening of enzyme inhibitors faces challenges such as low efficiency. In this study, a novel online HPLC-FLD/pancreatic lipase recognition system was developed for the first time. The optimal operating parameters were established as a flow rate of 1 mL/min, with excitation and emission wavelengths for pancreatic lipase set at 221 nm and 303 nm, respectively. The effectiveness of this system was validated using orlistat. Subsequently, this system was applied to Lycium ruthenicum, where two petunidin-based anthocyanins pancreatic lipase inhibitors were efficiently isolated using medium-pressure liquid chromatography. Molecular docking elucidated that compounds 1 and 2 interact with the serine residue of pancreatic lipase, exhibiting binding energies of -13.12 kcal/mol and -12.22 kcal/mol, respectively. Enzymatic assays showed that the half-maximal inhibitory concentrations of compounds 1 and 2 were 9.67 μM and 147.37 μM, respectively. These docking and inhibition results confirm the system for efficiently discovering pancreatic lipase inhibitors.

title: Corrigendum to “Exploring the salt taste-enhancing activity of key peptides and ultrafiltrated fractions from spent hen meat hydrolysate” [Food Chem. 492 (2025) 145444]
Zein/ferulic acid/sodium alginate ternary nanoparticles: characterization and application in stable Pickering emulsions
abstract: In this study, zein/ferulic acid nanoparticles (ZFs) and zein/ferulic acid/sodium alginate nanoparticles (ZFSs) were prepared using the anti-solvent method and employed to stabilize Pickering emulsions. Compared with ZFs, ZFSs exhibited better performance. Specifically, although the particle size increased from 186.4 nm to 202.9 nm, the polydispersity index decreased from 0.27 to 0.19. The zeta potential shifted from +30.88 mV to -46.01 mV, and the denaturation peak temperature increased from 101.0 °C to 135.0 °C. Furthermore, FTIR analysis suggested the presence of hydrogen bonds, electrostatic forces, and hydrophobic interactions in ZFSs. Rheological tests showed that ZFSs-stabilized Pickering emulsions exhibited enhanced shear-thinning behavior and a higher elastic modulus than those stabilized by ZFs. Storage experiments confirmed that the particle size of the ZFSs-stabilized Pickering emulsion only increased to 14.8 μm after 30 days, and the zeta potential remained stable at -46.1 mV.

title: Phenolic profile and antioxidant properties of thirty one apple cultivars grown under the same edaphoclimatic conditions
abstract: This study analyzes the antioxidant properties and phenolic composition of 31 apple ( Malus domestica Borkh.) cultivars from Alcobaça region of Portugal. While numerous studies have explored apple phenolics, very few have compared such a large number of cultivars grown in the same region, thereby eliminating the influence of edaphoclimatic factors and focusing more on the plants' genetic variability. By assessing different fruit parts—peel, seeds, and mesocarp—this research provides a comprehensive characterization of bioactive compound distribution. Ultra-High Performance Liquid Chromatography – Time of Flight – Mass Spectrometry was used to quantify 49 distinct phenolic compounds, while antioxidant activity was evaluated through DPPH radical scavenging and other relevant assays. Results confirm that peels contain the highest phenolic and flavonoid concentrations, reaching up to 185.3 μg of chlorogenic Acid per gram of fresh fruit followed by seeds, with mesocarp showing significantly lower levels. Cultivars such as Fujion, Redefu20, and Smeralda exhibited high phenolic content, totaling between 541.46 and 619.83 μg of phenolic compounds per gram of fresh fruit, while Bigbucks, Challenger, and Story Inored stood out for their antioxidant capacity. • Comparative study of 31 apple cultivars grown under the same edaphoclimatic conditions. • Peels and seeds showed the highest phenolic content and antioxidant capacity. • UHPLC-ToF-MS identified and quantified 49 phenolic compounds in different fruit parts. • Fujion, Redefu20, and Smeralda had the highest phenolic content among all cultivars. • Findings support the valorization of apple by-products in food, nutraceutical, and cosmetic industries.

title: A MOF-based portable fluorescent sensing platform for visualization assay of thiamethoxam via hydrogen bond-induced enhanced ICT
abstract: Turn-on metal-organic framework (MOF) fluorescence sensors based on hydrogen bonding-induced intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) are novel fluorescent sensing materials. These sensors enhance the ICT effect through intermolecular hydrogen bonding, enabling highly sensitive detection of specific molecules. However, fluorescence quenching induced by electron-withdrawing targets (EWT) significantly inhibits the ICT process, negatively impacting the signal-to-noise ratio and sensitivity of ICT fluorophores for accurate sensing. Here, we present a MOF probe (UiO-66-Cou) based on 7-(diethylamino)-2-oxo-2H-chromene-3-carboxaldehyde (Cou) and UiO-66-NH 2 (based on the Schiff base reaction), which can be used for the "turn-on" sensing of thiamethoxam (TH) in aqueous environments with an extremely low detection limit (0.588 fmol/L) and high fluorescence turn-on efficiency. UiO-66-Cou detected TH and reversed the fluorescence quenching induced by TH (EWT) by facilitating fluorescence turn-on through weak hydrogen bonding interactions between the molecules. The specific hydrogen bond (CH⋯O) effectively prevents the rotation of the CN bond, thus enabling fluorescence turn-on. More importantly, for this MOF with low fluorescence emission efficiency, subsequent modification by integrating ICT fluorophores significantly enhances its fluorescence performance and functionality. Additionally, UiO-66-Cou was integrated into polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) (UiO-66-Cou@PMMA) to prepare a portable detection device for the rapid and reliable detection of TH in vegetable and fruit samples. This post-modification strategy based on hydrogen bond enhanced ICT fluorophores is not only applicable to UiO-66-Cou, but can also be extended to other MOF based fluorescent probe systems with lower luminescence efficiency. By introducing suitable ICT fluorophores and hydrogen bond interactions, its fluorescence recognizability and sensing sensitivity can be significantly enhanced. In summary, this work provides an effective and scalable strategy for enhancing ICT fluorophores via hydrogen bonding.

title: Enhancing emulsion stability in pork bone soup: Exploring the synergistic effects of polysaccharides and high-pressure homogenization
abstract: The effects of the concentrations of three polysaccharides (xanthan gum, pectin, and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMCNa)) and homogenization pressures on the stability and structure of pork bone soup were investigated. Stability was assessed through color, TSI, sedimentation, particle size, zeta potential, and rheology, while microstructure and protein structure analysis revealed underlying mechanisms. Results showed 0.2 % xanthan gum, 0.15 % pectin, and 0.7 % CMC-Na preserved color, enhanced zeta potential, and reduced particle size/sedimentation. Pectin (0.15 %) formed a lamellar structure, coating oil droplets and adsorbing onto protein layers. Homogenization at 20 MPa further reduced TSI/sedimentation and created uniform dispersions of droplets, inducing protein unfolding and gel network formation. The 0.15 % pectin with 20 MPa homogenization emerged as the most effective and economically viable approach for producing stable bone soup, combining optimal interfacial stabilization with structural reinforcement. These findings provide practical insights for developing premium-quality bone soup products with enhanced shelf stability.

title: Amino acids, ferritin, and mineral oxalates in edible Salicornia patula young shoots: Chemical characterization and nutritional implications
abstract: Young edible shoots of Salicornia patula Duval Jouve, collected from six populations were profiled for nutrient and mineral content. HPLC revealed, for the first time, a sulfur-rich amino acid spectrum (19.3-21.8 %) and substantial lysine (5.1-8.4 %). XRD analysis identified calcium and magnesium oxalates, along with halite (NaCl) and sylvite (KCl), indicating a crystallization-based strategy for salt and mineral storage. SEM/TEM localized ferritin cores, confirming intracellular iron accumulation. ICP-MS showed sodium as the dominant mineral (60.2-215.7 g-kg -1 DW), followed by calcium, magnesium, potassium, and iron (each >2 g kg -1 DW). Our findings demonstrate that S. patula accumulates ferritin from the onset of germination, particularly in succulent stems and embryos. Its edible young shoots are a promising plant-based source of essential amino acids, ferritin-bound iron, and minerals. Including young shoots in the diet may contribute to micronutrient intake and nutritional resilience with minimal oxalate-related concerns if consumed moderately.

title: Portable point-of-care testing of food glutathione enabled by a high-performance sulfur-vacancy FeS mimetic enzyme
abstract: Glutathione (GSH) is a key bioactive substance that significantly influences food nutrition and safety. In this study, a novel colorimetric sensing platform was developed based on sulfur vacancy iron sulfide (SV-FeS) mimetic enzyme for rapid and quantitative detection of GSH in food samples. The mimetic enzyme features a three-dimensional (3D) micro-flower structure with high specific surface area, exhibiting exceptional peroxidase-like (POD-like) activity. The SV-FeS (pH = 3, 1h) mimetic enzyme demonstrates high substrate affinity with a low Michaelis constant (Kₘ) of 0.052 mM toward H 2 O 2 . In liquid-phase GSH detection, the sensor showed excellent linearity in the range of 5-100 μM (R 2 = 0.998) with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.38 μM. To meet point-of-care testing (POCT) requirements, a microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) integrated with a SV-FeS (pH = 3, 1 h) mimetic enzyme and a smartphone-based readout system was constructed. This sensor enables one-step GSH quantification within 5 min, achieving a linear range of 35-500 μM (R 2 = 0.990) and a LOD of 10.4 μM. In practical applications, the sensor demonstrated satisfactory performance with spiked recoveries of 95.5 %-102.5 %, relative standard deviation (RSD) below 8 %, and maintained stability for 15 days at 4 °C. This work provides an effective solution for on-site GSH detection in food quality and safety monitoring.

title: Targeting myofibril-bound serine protease inhibition to improve grass carp surimi gel properties with edible additives: Insights from molecular docking
abstract: Thermal degradation of surimi gels mediated by myofibril-bound serine protease (MBSP) occurs ubiquitously in practical processing. Here, we employed molecular docking and virtual screening, selecting curcumin, naringenin, hesperetin, and ethyl vanillin as top candidates for validation. Hesperetin and ethyl vanillin exhibited the strongest binding affinity and interact with the key catalytic region of MBSP, including Gly195 and Val204. Naringenin and hesperetin inhibited MBSP activity by 25% and effectively preserved myosin heavy chain integrity. More importantly, incorporating these compounds (0.05%, w/w) into grass carp surimi notably enhanced gel strength by more than 20% and improved texture (p < 0.05) with more compact gel microstructures. Sensory evaluation confirmed that naringenin and hesperetin improved surimi overall.
